Name: compression_erases_the_writer
Title: Compression Erases the Writer, Not the Gain: Abstraction Level of Transferred Experience Helps Only When Writer != Reader
Short Hypothesis: The benefit of compressing agent experience before transfer is an interaction with writer identity, not a main effect. For a reader consuming its own success-filtered pool, raw trajectories beat writer-compressed summaries and procedures at matched injected tokens; for a pool written by a different backbone the order reverses, because compression strips the writer-specific search, phrasing and binding content that only its author can imitate. The survey claim 'transferability rises with compression' (2604.15877) and the finding 'raw beats distilled skills' (2605.24117) are the two cells of one interaction: the sign of the raw-minus-compressed contrast is predicted by whether the writer is the reader, the writer's identity is undetectable at the procedure level, and stripping the writer's thoughts from raw traces moves self and foreign cells in opposite directions.
Related Work: 2604.15877 states the compression axis (memory -> skills -> rules) and asserts transferability rises with compression, with no experiment. 2605.24117 (SkillEvolBench) shows raw-trajectory reuse often beats distilled skills, but writer and reader are the same backbone and tokens are not matched. 2604.14004 (memory transfer learning, coding agents) finds high-level insights transfer and low-level traces cause negative transfer across domains, without naming model pairs, without a self-pool control and without token matching. 2605.12978 finds consolidated memories degrade relative to raw episodic ones, again same backbone. 2606.23127 (procedural memory benchmark, 382 enterprise tasks) reports that some skills transfer across backbones and others specialise, but does not manipulate abstraction level or compare against raw traces. 2608.07169 distils a teacher's trajectories into one hierarchical level for small students with no raw-trace or self-pool arm. Home literature: 2509.22230 (reasoning traces tailored to the student by filtering tokens improbable under it) gives the distributional-misalignment mechanism at training time; this proposal tests its in-context analogue. Archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied abstraction within one writer; here the writer is the manipulated variable and the claim is that the contrast flips sign with it.
Abstract: Two published positions on how experience should be stored for reuse contradict each other: a survey argues that transferability rises with compression, while a benchmark finds that raw trajectories beat distilled skills because abstraction discards state-contingent cues. Neither manipulates who wrote the experience. We propose that both are right in different cells of one design. On ALFWorld we build three pools from the same training games -- expert walkthroughs, Qwen3-32B's own successes, and EXAONE-4.0-32B's own successes (collected at the same episode budget) -- and have each writer compress its own pool to three levels: raw trajectories, per-item summaries, and per-type procedures, each injected at about 420 tokens. Two 32B readers of different families read every level of every pool through one fixed retriever, so the self cells and the foreign cells differ only in writer identity at matched capability. The estimand is the interaction: (raw - compressed) for the reader's own pool minus (raw - compressed) for a foreign pool, with the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader x level, all net of a static expert-written procedure prompt and a memory-free baseline. Every confirmatory cell runs 674 games x 6 seeds, so two-cell contrasts have about +-3 net half-width and the interaction about +-4.2, and every margin is at least twice the half-width of its contrast. We predict raw wins in self cells by at least 6 net, compression wins in foreign cells by at least 6, an interaction of at least 8 net, that at the procedure level a reader cannot tell its own procedures from a stranger's (equivalence within +-6) and neither beats the static prompt, that re-compressing the foreign pool with the reader itself changes nothing (what matters is what compression removes, not who words it), and, as the mechanism test, that stripping the writer's thoughts from raw trajectories costs the reader's own pool more than it costs a stranger's pool. A null or reversed interaction, raw winning in a foreign cell, or thoughts that are equally dispensable for both writers falsifies the account and settles the survey's claim negatively for this domain.
Experiments: Domain and partition: ALFWorld. Bank = the 3,553 training games minus a held-out slice of 400 training games excluded from every pool; evaluation = 274 validation games (140 seen, 134 unseen) + the 400 held-out training games = 674 games per seed. Retriever fixed (Measurement A's); retrieval is deterministic per game, so every cell at a level sees the same retrieved game ids across seeds and cells. Writers: E = expert walkthroughs (1,465, minus held-out); Q = Qwen3-32B self pool (1,892 successes, minus held-out); X = EXAONE-4.0-32B self pool, collected on the same 3,553 training games at the same scaffold and temperature (about 3 GPU-hours), success-filtered. Levels, produced by the writer model itself from its own pool: L0 raw trajectory (k=3, about 430 tokens, as measured); L1 per-item summary (4-6 lines keeping object and receptacle names, about 70 tokens, k=6); L2 per-type procedure (one paragraph per task type distilled from the writer's own pool, all six injected, about 420 tokens). Compressor identity: writer-compressed versions (Q pool by Qwen3, X pool by EXAONE) are primary; the reader-compressed versions of the foreign pool (X pool by Qwen3 for the Qwen3 reader, Q pool by EXAONE for the EXAONE reader) at L1 and L2 form the compressor-identity arm. For E, which has no writer model, the compressor is the non-reader backbone so E stays fully foreign. Thought-stripped raw (L0s): the L0 items with thoughts removed, actions and observations kept including failed steps, template-normalised; at matched tokens k rises to about 5. Readers: Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B (family mismatch at approximately matched capability; both serving to be verified in vLLM before the first confirmatory cell). Cells per reader, primary at 6 seeds (674 x 6 = 4,044 episodes per cell): k=0; static expert six-procedure prompt (Measurement C); self L0, L1, L2; foreign L0, L1, L2 (writer-compressed); foreign L1 and L2 reader-compressed; self L0s; foreign L0s = 12 cells = 48,528 episodes. Secondary at 2 seeds (1,348 per cell): E L0; E L2 (non-reader-compressed); self L1 and foreign L1 at k=3 (k-matched); self L0 and foreign L0 from type-balanced pools = 6 cells = 8,088 episodes. Per reader 56,616 episodes; both readers 113,232 episodes. Throughput: about 18 episodes/min per replica, one replica per A100; each reader's cells run on their own GPU in parallel, about 52 h each; GPU1 first collects the X pool (3 h); compression is batched (each backbone compresses Q, X and E at L1 and L2: 12 short jobs, about 1-2 h total). Wall-clock about 2.5 days. Order on each GPU: the six headline cells (k=0, static, self L0, self L2, foreign L0, foreign L2) first, then the L1 cells, then the compressor-identity cells, then the stripped cells, then the secondary cells, so every confirmatory contrast is complete before any secondary cell starts; if EXAONE serves slower, GPU0 switches to a second EXAONE replica when the Qwen3 cells finish. Estimands: net gain over k=0 paired by game and seed; D(w,r,L) = gain(L0) - gain(L) for L in {L1, L2}; interaction I(r) = D(self) - D(foreign) at the pre-registered level; stripping interaction S(r) = [gain(self L0) - gain(self L0s)] - [gain(foreign L0) - gain(foreign L0s)]; retained-gain ratio per writer x reader x level with two denominators (the writer's own gain from the same pool, and the reader's self-pool gain at the same level), on gains over k=0, with cluster-bootstrap CIs, reported only where the denominator's CI excludes 0; everything also reported net of the static prompt. Manipulation checks (not predictions): token counts per level within +-10%; textual divergence between the two writers' L1 and L2 sets (embedding similarity and normalised edit distance per type) with a pre-registered rule: if the writers' L2 procedures are near-identical (normalised edit distance below 0.2 per type), L1 replaces L2 as the level of P1 and P3, and the first clause of P5 is reported as a manipulation-check outcome rather than a finding; per-type composition of each pool. Pre-registration of gates, margins, the level rule and the seed rule before the first confirmatory cell. Optional, outside the envelope above and only if the primary cells finish early: Qwen3-8B as a same-family lower-capability writer for the Qwen3 reader at L0 and L2 (2 cells at 2 seeds, about 1.5 GPU-h of collection), a descriptive capability-at-fixed-proximity arm.
Baselines and Ablations: Memory-free k=0 per reader (6 seeds). Static expert-written six-procedure prompt (Measurement C) per reader (6 seeds): every gain also reported net of it. Self-pool control at matched collection cost is built in (Q->Qwen3 and X->EXAONE, both from the same 3,553-game budget at the same scaffold and temperature). Compressor identity: foreign pool compressed by the writer vs by the reader at L1 and L2 (6 seeds; carries P4). Thought-stripped raw (L0s) for self and foreign pools at matched tokens (6 seeds; carries P6): separates the writer's phrasing from its actions and search. Expert pool E at L0 and L2 (2 seeds): a foreign writer with no search and no thoughts, descriptive. k-matched L1 (k=3) vs token-matched L1 (k=6, primary) for self and foreign (2 seeds). Type-balanced pools (equal per-type counts) for self and foreign L0 (2 seeds), because the self pools are type-skewed. Type-stratified (clean/heat/cool vs pick/look/pick-two) and seen vs unseen estimates reported for every primary contrast. Cut from the previous version to fit the envelope: the E re-compressed-by-reader cells, E L1, and the gpt-oss-120b writer arm; the optional Qwen3-8B writer replaces the latter as a cheaper capability-at-fixed-proximity arm.
Falsifiable Predictions: Planning noise (see Measurement): two-cell contrasts between 6-seed cells have 95% half-width about +-3 net; four-cell contrasts about +-4.2. Margins are fractions of Measurement A's +27 (6 = 0.22, 8 = 0.3) and each is at least twice the half-width of its contrast. P1 (self cells, raw wins): D(self, L2) = gain(raw) - gain(writer-written procedures) >= +6 net at matched tokens, separately in Q->Qwen3 and in X->EXAONE; D(self, L1) >= +6 likewise. Each of the four contrasts is scored on its own: falsified if its 95% CI includes 0 or its upper bound is below +6 (a null D(self) ~ 0 gives a CI of about [-3, +3] and falsifies). Produced by the self L0, L1, L2 cells at 6 seeds. P2 (foreign cells, compression wins): D(foreign, L1) <= -6 and D(foreign, L2) <= -6 net, separately in X->Qwen3 and in Q->EXAONE. Each of the four contrasts is scored on its own: falsified if its 95% CI includes 0 or its lower bound is above -6; raw foreign winning in any single cell falsifies that cell. Produced by the foreign L0, L1, L2 (writer-compressed) cells at 6 seeds. P3 (headline interaction): I(r) = D(self) - D(foreign) >= +8 net with a 95% CI excluding 0, for each reader, at the pre-registered level (L2, or L1 under the convergence rule). Falsified if the CI includes 0 or I(r) is negative for either reader; a null gives a CI of about [-4.2, +4.2]. Produced by the four cells self-L0, self-L2, foreign-L0, foreign-L2 for that reader. P4 (what is removed, not who words it): for each reader and each of L1, L2, gain(reader-compressed foreign) - gain(writer-compressed foreign) is zero within +-6. Confirmed only if the 95% CI lies inside [-6, +6] and includes 0; falsified if the 95% CI excludes 0 in either direction (reader wording helping or hurting; a true difference of 6 gives a CI of about [3, 9]); otherwise inconclusive and 4 seeds are added to the cells of that contrast. Produced by the compressor-identity cells against the writer-compressed foreign cells at 6 seeds. P5 (the writer is erased at L2): for each reader, gain(self L2) - gain(foreign L2) is zero within +-6 (confirmed only if the 95% CI lies inside [-6, +6] and includes 0), and neither L2 cell beats the static expert prompt. Falsified if self-L2 differs from foreign-L2 with a 95% CI excluding 0 in either direction, or if either L2 cell exceeds the static prompt with a 95% CI entirely above 0 (the rival account, writer identity as a main effect at every level, produces exactly this). Produced by the self L2, foreign L2 and static cells at 6 seeds. P6 (the removed content is the writer's search and phrasing): the stripping interaction S(r) = [gain(self L0) - gain(self L0s)] - [gain(foreign L0) - gain(foreign L0s)] >= +6 net with a 95% CI excluding 0 for each reader: removing thoughts costs the reader's own pool more than it costs the foreign pool, and the point prediction is that the foreign half is negative (stripped foreign beats raw foreign). Falsified if the CI of S(r) includes 0 or S(r) is negative (thoughts are filler or noise regardless of who wrote them). Produced by the self L0, self L0s, foreign L0, foreign L0s cells at 6 seeds. The retained-gain ratio is reported per writer x reader x level with bootstrap CIs as the estimand the brief requires; no prediction is stated on it because ratio(L2) > ratio(L0) is arithmetic on the cell means that already decide P1 and P2.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design: every cell runs the same 674 games with the same seeds, retriever and sampling settings as Measurement A; cells differ only in writer, level, compressor and reader. Planning noise scales the brief's +-8 net at 274 x 2 seeds (548 episodes) by 1/sqrt(episodes): a 6-seed cell (4,044 episodes) has per-cell net-gain half-width about +-2.9; a two-cell contrast (D, the P4 and P5 differences) about +-3; a four-cell contrast (I, S) about +-4.2; 2-seed secondary cells +-5.1. Every margin is at least twice the planning half-width of its contrast (6 vs 3; 8 vs 4.2), so the predicted outcome and the null give non-overlapping CIs. Seeds are fixed at 6 in advance, not escalated on demand; the pre-registered amendment is that if the bootstrap half-width of any primary contrast exceeds +-4 (two-cell) or +-5.5 (four-cell), 4 more seeds are added to every cell of that contrast before its point estimate is inspected. Mixed-effects logistic model with game random effects and cluster bootstrap over games (seeds nested in games) for all contrasts and ratios. Type-stratified estimates alongside. Injected token counts logged per episode and matched within +-10%; retrieval results logged so that every cell at a level sees the same retrieved game ids. Margins as fractions of the Gate-0 effect: Measurement A's +27 net is the reference; +6 is 0.22 of it, +8 is 0.3. Unseen-only claims carry the 134-game CI and are reported as secondary.

No collision found; the nearest, 2604.14004 and 2605.24117, occupy one cell each of the proposed interaction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: EXAONE-4.0-32B serving in vLLM is unverified; fallback is gpt-oss-120b as the second backbone (then family and capability are confounded and the claim is reported as foreign-writer only) or a second Qwen3-32B scaffold as a proximity-only foreign writer. P1 may fail (compression free even for the reader's own pool), which refutes 2605.24117 in this domain and is reportable, but then the interaction is a main effect of level and the title claim falls; P2 may fail (raw foreign wins), which settles the survey's claim negatively and also kills the title claim. P1 with P5 implies that the reader's own raw traces beat the expert static prompt, and P2 with P5 implies that a stranger's raw traces fall below it; both implications are exposed to the data in the same cells. L2 texts from different writers may converge, making L2 uninformative for the writer contrast; the convergence rule moves P1 and P3 to L1 and demotes the first clause of P5 to a manipulation check. The self pools are type-skewed towards easy types; the type-balanced ablation guards against a composition artefact. The thought-stripped arm changes k (about 5 at matched tokens); the stripping interaction S(r) cancels the k effect to first order, not exactly. ALFWorld procedures are short and the ceiling at k=3 is near 0.87 on unseen, so gains are bounded above; margins are set as fractions of the measured +27. Two 32B families approximate matched capability but their k=0 rates will differ; the retained-gain ratio uses each reader's own self-pool gain as one denominator to absorb this. Budget: 113k episodes at 18 episodes/min per replica is about 52 h per GPU; if measured throughput is lower the secondary cells are cut first, then the L1 cells of P1 (L2 stays), never the seeds of the headline cells. Capability at fixed proximity is only an optional descriptive arm (Qwen3-8B writer); the design manipulates proximity (family) at approximately fixed capability.
Addresses gap: G10 (compression-transferability claim untested against raw-beats-skills at matched inference cost), with G6 (same-backbone evaluation) as the manipulated variable.
Not a restatement of: Brief prior-result bullet Measurement A (expert raw k=3 gives +27/+32 net; unseen approx seen, procedure-bound): it measured one foreign writer at one level; this idea claims the sign of the raw-vs-compressed contrast depends on whether the writer is the reader, which no single-writer measurement can show. Digest card arxiv:2604.14004 (high-level insights transfer, low-level traces cause negative transfer): it reports a cross-domain main effect of abstraction with unnamed model pairs and no self-pool; this idea claims the low-level harm exists only for foreign-written traces and reverses into a benefit for the reader's own traces at matched tokens. Archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied level within one writer; this idea fixes level and swaps the writer, and the interaction is the estimand.
Changes made: P1: margin raised from +4 to +6 and seeds raised from 2 to 6 on all self cells (two-cell half-width about +-3, so a null D ~ 0 now falsifies); falsifier restated as 'CI includes 0 or upper bound below +6', scored per cell and per level. P2: same seeds and margin (-6); falsifier made per cell and per level instead of conjunctive over both foreign cells; the L1 cells are in the 6-seed set. P3: unchanged as the headline, now at 6 seeds (half-width about +-4.2 against the +8 margin) with a fixed seed count instead of an on-demand escalation. P4: recast as a two-sided zero-within-+-6 test on the compressor-identity cells at 6 seeds; a reader-compressed version that is worse, not only better, now falsifies, and a wide CI no longer confirms; the E re-compressed cells were cut. P5: recast from a universal null into an equivalence test (self-L2 vs foreign-L2 zero within +-6, either direction falsifies) plus a per-cell falsifier against the static prompt (any L2 cell whose CI lies above 0 falsifies); this sharpens the claim: at L2 the reader cannot tell its own procedures from a stranger's. P6: the retained-gain-ratio prediction was removed as arithmetic on the P1/P2 cell means; the ratio stays as the reported estimand with bootstrap CIs and two denominators. It is replaced by a mechanism prediction with its own cells: the thought-stripping interaction S(r) (removing thoughts costs the self pool more than the foreign pool), which tests the stated mechanism, that what compression removes is the writer's search and phrasing and only its author can use it, rather than a consequence of P1 and P2. Budget arithmetic: 12 primary cells per reader at 674 games x 6 seeds = 48,528 episodes plus 6 secondary cells at 2 seeds = 8,088, so 56,616 per reader and 113,232 total; at 18 episodes/min per replica that is about 52 h per GPU with the two readers served in parallel, plus 3 GPU-h for the X pool and 1-2 h of compression, about 2.5 days wall-clock. Cut to fit: E L1, the E re-compressed cells, the gpt-oss-120b arm (replaced by an optional Qwen3-8B same-family writer at 2 cells, outside the envelope). The central claim was not softened: the sign flip of raw-minus-compressed with writer identity remains the headline, its margins went up (4 -> 6) rather than down, and two sharper falsifiable claims were added (P5: writer indistinguishable at L2; P6: thoughts are author-specific), each with a null that the design can reach and distinguish at the stated noise.

Name: leave_one_type_out_split
Title: Within-Type Splits Inflate Transfer: A Leave-One-Type-Out Composite Shows Retrieval Gains Are Type-Bound, Harm Tracks Within-Type Gain, and Only Weights Carry Portable Competence
Short Hypothesis: The standard ALFWorld splits (valid_seen/valid_unseen) always leave same-type items in the bank, so every measured transfer gain is procedure retrieval. Under a leave-one-type-out (LOTO) composite, in which each of the 274 validation games is read against a bank lacking its own task type, retrieval gains from every writer collapse below +8 net, and the writer that helps most within-type (the off-policy expert, whose items the reader follows most closely) becomes harmful under type shift while the reader's own pool stays near neutral. The harm is a following behaviour, not a knowledge deficit, so it survives even when the missing competence is put into the weights. Absorbing the same expert pool into QLoRA adapters, evaluated with the matching LOTO adapter, retains a positive type-portable gain (navigation and action validity) net of a five-procedure static prompt, so the retrieval-versus-weights ranking flips between splits at matched cost.
Related Work: PAST-Bench (arxiv:2608.04003) toggles retained experience and S3Gym (arxiv:2608.31100) compares history ICL, summaries and training, but neither holds out a task type or swaps the writer. AgentCL (arxiv:2606.02461) builds controlled task streams for continual learning without cross-writer or held-out-type transfer. Retrieval-aware fine-tuning (arxiv:2603.18272) claims generalization to unseen tasks but does not compare retrieval and weights under the same held-out split with writer identity manipulated. Parametric memories (PEAM arxiv:2605.27762; fast-weight memory arxiv:2606.04536) assert efficiency and portability on one environment and backbone (digest gap G25). MemHarness (arxiv:2607.28272) shows verbatim replay of retrieved experience causes negative transfer out of distribution, on self-written experience and without a weights arm, so it cannot say whether the harm persists once the competence is in the weights. In the home literature, in-context learning with mismatched demonstrations is known to hurt or help depending on evidence mixture (arxiv:2605.26350) and cross-task demonstration transfer can help (CrossICL arxiv:2505.24143), but no work couples the harm of wrong-task demonstrations to how strongly the same demonstrations help in-task, across demonstrators. Measurement A on this node found unseen ~ seen with the full bank (a room split, not a type split) and Measurement B provides the QLoRA arm. Archived context_wins_substrate_conflict (5.55) concerned substrate conflict within-type; here the split, not the conflict, is the manipulated variable.
Abstract: Transfer of agent experience is evaluated on splits that keep same-type experience in the bank, so the gain reported is the gain of finding a same-type procedure. We propose a leave-one-type-out (LOTO) composite for ALFWorld: six banks each missing one task type, and every one of the 274 validation games read against the bank that lacks its type, giving one full-size cell per writer x reader instead of six under-powered per-type cells. Writer identity is manipulated (expert walkthroughs; Qwen3-32B's own successes; EXAONE-4.0-32B's own successes at the same collection budget) with one retriever and one item format; readers are Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B. The same expert pool is absorbed into QLoRA rank-32 adapters (one all-type adapter as in Measurement B and six LOTO adapters), served by vLLM multi-LoRA so the adapter composite runs as one cell; adapters are evaluated memory-absent, matched (their own pool) and mismatched (the self pool). Controls: k=0, six- and five-procedure static prompts (the LOTO analog of Measurement C), a random-other-type token-matched placebo, and a wrong-procedure graft at 100% as the Gate-0 positive control. The cells that carry the claims run at 8 seeds (MDE +/-4 net) and every prediction has one pre-registered decision boundary with the hypothesis and its named rival each at least one MDE from it. Predictions: LOTO retrieval gain below +8 for every writer whose within-type gain is at least +16 (headline: the expert pool in the Qwen3 reader, predicted -8); the expert pool at least 6 net worse than the self pool under LOTO and at least 4 net below k=0; the LOTO adapter at least +6 over the five-procedure prompt and at least +12 over LOTO retrieval of the same pool, while within-type retrieval beats the all-type adapter by at least +8; and the expert items still cost at least 4 net when retrieved on top of the matching LOTO adapter, so the harm is a following behaviour rather than a knowledge deficit. Estimands: within-type gain, LOTO gain, their paired difference (the type-bound fraction), the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader under each split, and cost per net point for weights versus retrieval. About 28,300 episodes plus 17 GPU-hours of collection and training, two days on two A100s.
Experiments: Preparation (about half a day): render pools by env replay; construct six LOTO banks per writer keyed on the ALFWorld task-type label (pick-two and pick-and-place recorded as a skeleton-similar pair; a seventh bank excludes both); build the wrong-procedure graft pool (each item's appliance step swapped to the wrong appliance, replay-checked to fail); build the five-procedure static prompt per target type (target type's procedure omitted, token-matched to k=3). Collection on GPU1: EXAONE-4.0-32B k=0 pool on the train split at the same episode budget as the existing Qwen3-32B self pool (about 3 GPU-hours). Training on GPU1 while GPU0 serves: seven QLoRA r32 adapters on the expert pool (six LOTO adapters first, then the all-type adapter as in Measurement B; about 2 GPU-hours each, 14 GPU-hours), served through vLLM multi-LoRA on the bf16 base with per-request adapter selection so each adapter composite is one cell. Reader cells, all 274 validation games, episodes = 274 x seeds. Qwen3-32B reader, k=3 unless noted: [1] k=0, 8 seeds, 2,192; [2] five-procedure static prompt, 8 seeds, 2,192; [3] LOTO expert, 8 seeds, 2,192; [4] LOTO self, 8 seeds, 2,192; [5] LOTO EXAONE-writer, 4 seeds, 1,096; [6] standard expert (Measurement A's 2 seeds plus 2 new), 548 new; [7] standard self, 4 seeds, 1,096; [8] standard EXAONE-writer, 2 seeds, 548; [9] random-other-type placebo, 2 seeds, 548; [10] wrong-procedure graft at 100%, 4 seeds, 1,096 (Gate 0); [11] joint-exclusion bank (pick-two and pick-and-place removed together), expert writer, on the roughly 90 games of those two types, 4 seeds, about 360; [12] LOTO adapter composite, memory-absent, 8 seeds, 2,192; [13] all-type adapter, memory-absent, 4 seeds, 1,096; [14] LOTO adapter + LOTO expert retrieval (matched), 8 seeds, 2,192; [15] all-type adapter + standard expert retrieval (matched), 2 seeds, 548; [16] LOTO adapter + LOTO self retrieval (mismatched), 4 seeds, 1,096. Qwen3 subtotal about 21,200 episodes. EXAONE-4.0-32B reader (4-seed replication): [17] k=0, 4 seeds, 1,096; [18] five-procedure static, 4 seeds, 1,096; [19] six-procedure static (Measurement C analog), 2 seeds, 548; [20] LOTO expert, 4 seeds, 1,096; [21] LOTO own, 4 seeds, 1,096; [22] LOTO Qwen3-writer, 2 seeds, 548; [23-25] standard expert, own, Qwen3-writer, 2 seeds each, 1,644. EXAONE subtotal about 7,100. Total about 28,300 episodes; at the sibling measurements' rate of about 1,100 episodes per replica-hour at saturating concurrency, about 26 replica-hours. Schedule: hours 0-13 GPU0 serves the Qwen3 base reader (cells 1-11, about 14,100 episodes) while GPU1 collects (3 h) then trains (14 h); the roughly 2-hour gap before the six LOTO adapters land at hour 15 is filled by the optional k=1 ablation cells; hours 15-21.5 GPU0 runs the adapter cells (12, 14, 16, then 13 and 15 once the all-type adapter lands at hour 17; about 7,100 episodes); hours 17-23.5 GPU1 serves the EXAONE reader (about 7,100 episodes). About 24 serving wall-hours plus preparation: about 2 days, both GPUs busy throughout. Per cell: success, net vs k=0 and vs the appropriate static prompt, per type, seen/unseen, injected tokens, steps, retained-gain ratio, and cost per net point (collection GPU-hours, training GPU-hours, consumer tokens).

Name: own_errors_pass_the_gate
Title: The Reader Cannot Grade Its Own Homework: Self-Authored Contamination Evades Read-Time Detection in Agent Experience Stores
Short Hypothesis: A reader asked to verify retrieved experience before acting misses planted errors more often when the host trajectory was written by itself than when the identical error is planted in a trajectory written by another backbone, because self-authored text is familiar (low perplexity under the reader) and LLM judges favour familiar text. Consequently the same planted error, once retrieved, costs the reader more success when its host is self-written than when it is foreign-written; an external reference (a static procedure prompt) closes at least half of the detection gap; and a content detector keeps most of the legitimate foreign gain that a writer-identity gate discards by construction.
Related Work: Self-preference in LLM evaluation is established outside agents: 2404.13076 (evaluators recognise and favour their own generations), 2410.21819 (bias tracks familiarity measured by perplexity), 2504.03846 (harmful vs legitimate self-preference on verifiable tasks), 2402.11436 (self-bias in self-refinement, reduced by external feedback). None applies it to verifying retrieved action trajectories or measures downstream task harm; the paraphrase 2x2 here (the same item rewritten by the reader or by the other backbone) transfers 2410.21819's perplexity manipulation to action trajectories with content held fixed. Memory contamination work is adversarial and single-backbone: 2512.16962 MemoryGraft (benign-looking implanted experiences, no defence), 2605.22842 (trust laundering, policy-formatted documents), 2608.11888 (seemingly relevant skills cause failures, author-reader mismatch not examined), 2601.05504 (attack/defence with trust-threshold calibration), 2510.02373 A-MemGuard (consensus validation), 2608.03509 SkillJack, 2607.06595, 2602.15654. None manipulates authorship of the contaminated item, none scores a reader-side detector by precision and recall against planted labels, and none costs its defence on non-adversarial foreign content (G9). Archived lineage_blast_radius (4.75) concerned consolidation laundering low-trust experience under a provenance rule and was judged entailed by that rule; here there is no consolidation rule, the detector is the reader's own judgement and its false-positive cost on clean foreign items is measured.
Abstract: Whether an agent can tell a helpful retrieved experience from a harmful one at read time is unmeasured, and every memory-poisoning study plants its poison in a single backbone's store. We ask a sharper question: does detection depend on who wrote the contaminated item? The self-preference literature shows LLM judges favour text they could have produced themselves, with bias tracking perplexity. We import that mechanism into experience verification. On ALFWorld we take success-filtered pools written by Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B, an expert planner and a second Qwen3-32B scaffold, and apply one scripted edit rule to each -- a procedure graft (heat steps swapped for cool steps under a heat task), a wrong final receptacle, and, as an ecological family, the writer's own failures relabelled as successes -- so that error content is identical across writers and only authorship differs. Each reader verifies retrieved items before acting; we score precision and recall against planted labels in a reader x host-writer cross design on game-paired items, so a pool-difficulty main effect is separated from an authorship interaction. We predict recall at least 10 points lower on self-authored hosts; that rewriting foreign items with the reader itself, but not with the other backbone, lowers their detection by at least 8 points once their perplexity matches self-written items; that a static procedure prompt in the verifier at least halves the gap; and that the same planted error, once retrieved, costs at least 5 more net points when its host is self-written than when it is foreign-written. Downstream cells with and without the detector as a gate, on contaminated and on clean multi-writer stores, put the defence's cost on legitimate foreign transfer in the same units as the harm it prevents.
Experiments: Domain and partition as in Measurement A with the 400-game held-out training slice added: 674 evaluation games per downstream cell, k=3 retrieval within task type, retriever fixed as in Measurement A. Pools (hosts), each collected on the about 3,100 remaining training games under the same rule (one attempt per game plus a second attempt on games failed at the first, success-filtered; about 4 GPU-h per collected pool, matched budget): Q = Qwen3-32B, X = EXAONE-4.0-32B (shared with sibling proposals), E = expert walkthroughs, S' = Qwen3-32B under a second scaffold at temperature 1.0 (same backbone, lower proximity; verification cells only), plus each model's failed trajectories for family C3. Contamination families applied by one script identically to every host pool: C1 procedure graft (manipulation sub-sequence of type T replaced by that of type T' with room-consistent receptacle names; task and label stay T); C2 receptacle swap (final put target replaced by a plausible wrong receptacle of the same room); C3 natural errors (the writer's own failures relabelled as successes; content varies by writer by nature). A hard C1 variant (a single omitted or wrong step, e.g. no 'open fridge') is pre-registered if C1 recall exceeds 80% on both hosts. The headline family is chosen by the pre-registered 30-80% foreign-recall rule on a 100-item pilot per (reader, host, family). Detectors: before acting, the reader judges each retrieved item ('does this trajectory correctly solve its stated task? yes/no, one-line reason'); D0 zero-shot; D1 with the Measurement C static six-procedure prompt in the verification context; D-consensus majority of three D0 samples (A-MemGuard-style named baseline); D-NLL non-LLM baseline flagging the top-x% items by the reader's per-token NLL. Verification cells: headline family at >= 1500 planted and >= 1500 clean items per (reader, host) for hosts {Q, X, E, S'} x readers {Qwen3, EXAONE}, every item scored under both D0 and D1 (identical paired item sets); D-consensus on a 600/600 subset of the Q and X hosts; non-headline families at 600/600 on Q and X under D0 and D1; format-normalised arm (thoughts stripped to actions and observations) on Q and X under D0; prompt-position ablation for the Qwen3 reader; per-item reader NLL from vLLM prompt logprobs for every item (manipulation check: self-authored hosts have lower NLL; entailed, not a prediction). Paraphrase 2x2 on each reader's foreign-host headline items (1500 planted + 600 clean): every item rewritten by the reader itself and, separately, by the other backbone, best-of-4 by the paraphraser's own NLL, script-verified that the planted error survives and length within +-20% of the original; a self-paraphrase qualifies if its per-token NLL under the reader is at or below the 75th percentile of that reader's self-host items (qualifying fraction reported; if fewer than 1300 planted pairs qualify, best-of-8 on the remainder, then additional edited pool trajectories); all paraphrased versions re-scored under D0. Verification volume: about 113k short calls (about 1k prompt tokens, 30 output tokens: 48k headline D0+D1, 14k consensus, 19k other families, 12k format-normalised, 6k prompt-position, 8k paraphrase re-scoring, 5k pilot) plus about 34k paraphrase generations, about 10-14 replica-hours split by reader across the two replicas. Downstream cells (674 games; bank rates within the retrieved task type; expected contaminated items among k=3 are 0/0.9/1.5 at 0/30/50%): the Gate-0 pair first (rate 0 and 50% C1, Q hosts, Qwen3 reader); C1 rate block rates {0, 30, 50%} x hosts {Q, X}: Qwen3 reader at 6 seeds (6 x 674 x 6 = 24,264 episodes; carries P1 and P5), EXAONE reader at 2 seeds (6 x 1,348 = 8,088; replication); a 100% Q->Qwen3 cell at 2 seeds (1,348) only if Gate 0 fails at 50%; D0-gated arms at 30% (flagged items dropped and refilled from the next retrieved rank) for hosts {Q, X} x both readers at 2 seeds (5,392); clean rate-0 three-writer mixed store (Q+X+E) with no gate, D0 gate and D1 gate: Qwen3 reader at 4 seeds (8,088; carries P6), EXAONE reader at 2 seeds (4,044); k=0 and static-prompt baselines per reader at 2 seeds (5,392). The writer-identity gate on the mixed store (drop all foreign, refill from self) coincides with the rate-0 self-host cell under the same retriever, so it is not run again; its cost is the mixed-minus-self difference with a CI. Total about 55k episodes (56.5k with the contingent 100% cell); at Measurement A's throughput of about 1,000 episodes per hour per replica this is about 55 replica-hours, plus 10-14 replica-hours of verification and paraphrase calls and about 8 GPU-h of pool collection (X, S'): about 75 replica-hours, about 2 days on two A100s. Scheduling: replica A serves Qwen3-32B (S' collection, Qwen3-reader verification, then its downstream cells), replica B serves EXAONE (X collection, EXAONE-reader verification, its downstream cells) and switches to serving Qwen3 when its queue empties so neither GPU idles; client concurrency is tuned to the vLLM running queue. Optional capability arm (gpt-oss-120b as third reader on its own pool, 3 GPU-h) only if time remains. Gates, margins, the Gate-0 interim rule and amendments are pre-registered before the first confirmatory cell.
Baselines and Ablations: No detector (plain retrieval) at every rate. D-NLL familiarity baseline (expected worst on self hosts: it encodes the bias). D-consensus (A-MemGuard-style self-consistency) on a 600/600 subset. D1 (external reference) vs D0 on identical item sets. Writer-identity gate on the clean mixed store as the provenance-style comparator, computed as mixed-minus-self (it coincides with the rate-0 self cell under the same retriever) and reported with a CI. Families C1, C2, C3 and the hard C1 variant. Host E, foreign to both readers: the two readers' recall on E should agree, a check that the self-foreign gap is not a reader main effect. Host S', same backbone as the Qwen3 reader under a second scaffold and temperature 1.0: proximity varied at fixed capability; its recall is expected to fall between the Q and X hosts in the order of reader NLL and is reported as a familiarity dose-response for P3 without a separate prediction. Format normalisation (thoughts stripped to actions and observations) for Q and X hosts, to separate authorship recognition by format from familiarity of content. Paraphrase 2x2 (paraphraser self vs other backbone; planted vs clean items). Detector prompt position (item before or after the task) for the Qwen3 reader. Type-stratified precision and recall, and false-positive rate by host for every detector. Memory-free and static-prompt baselines per reader; every gain reported net of the static prompt; retained-gain ratio of the clean foreign cells vs self reported per writer x reader with CIs as context for G9.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (Gate 0): C1 at 50% bank rate in Q->Qwen3 reduces net success by >= 6 points vs the rate-0 bank (same games, seeds and retrieval ranks; paired half-width about +-2.5 at 6 seeds; the decision is taken after the first 2 seeds unless the estimate lies within +-3 of the margin, in which case the remaining seeds are run first). Falsified if harm < 6 at 50% and at 100% (contingent 100% cell); produced by the Q-host rate cells of the Qwen3 reader. P2 (headline authorship effect): D0 recall on headline-family items is >= 10 points lower on self-authored hosts than on foreign-authored hosts for each reader, and the reader x host-writer interaction (the sum of the two readers' foreign-minus-self gaps over game-paired items) has a 95% CI excluding 0; at 1500/1500 items per cell recall SE is about 1.3, each gap SE about 1.8 and the interaction SE about 2.6, so the 10-point margin is about twice the half-width. Falsified if recall(self host) >= recall(foreign host) for either reader, or if both readers show the same host ordering (a pool-difficulty main effect with no interaction); produced by the 2x2 D0 cells {Qwen3, EXAONE} x {Q hosts, X hosts}. P3 (familiarity mediates, paraphrase 2x2): on the NLL-qualifying self-paraphrases (per-token reader NLL at or below the 75th percentile of self-host items; >= 1300 within-item pairs; qualifying fraction reported), (a) paired D0 recall is >= 8 points below the unparaphrased originals, and (b) the self-paraphrase drop exceeds the cross-paraphrase drop (the same originals rewritten by the other backbone, reader NLL not lowered) by >= 5 points. Falsified for (a) if the paired drop's 95% CI (half-width about +-3) has upper bound < 4, a region that contains the whole +-3 equivalence band around zero, or if paraphrased items are detected more often; falsified for (b) if the difference of the two paired drops (half-width about +-4) has upper bound < 5, the outcome produced when paraphrasing as such, not familiarity, lowers detection; produced by the paraphrase cells on P2's foreign-host items. P4 (external reference closes the gap): on identical item sets scored under both detectors, D1 raises self-host recall by >= 8 points for each reader (within-item paired half-width about +-3), and gap_D1 <= 0.5 x gap_D0. Falsified if the paired self-host lift has 95% CI upper bound < 4 for either reader, or if gap_D1 - 0.5 x gap_D0 has a game-paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0 from above (D1 lifting both hosts equally produces exactly this); the gap clause is scored only if P2's D0 gap is >= 10 for that reader, otherwise only the lift clause is scored; produced by the D0 and D1 cells. P5 (per-retrieval harm): in the Qwen3 reader's 30% and 50% C1 cells (6 seeds), each episode that retrieved >= 1 planted item is paired with its rate-0 twin (same game, seed and retrieval ranks; only the planted items' content differs); the paired success loss is >= 5 net points larger on the self host Q than on the foreign host X (about 6,200 pairs per host; half-width about +-1.7 per host and +-2.4 on the difference after a game design effect of about 1.5, so the margin is at least twice the half-width and 0.8 of the Gate-0 minimum). Falsified if the game-clustered bootstrap CI of the self-minus-foreign loss has upper bound < 5, which includes every world in which foreign-written errors harm as much as or more than self-written ones; produced by the rate {0, 30, 50%} x host {Q, X} cells of the Qwen3 reader; the conditioning on retrieval uses the retrieval log, which is identical in both arms, so it selects the same (game, seed) pairs in both. Leverage (loss over clean gain) is reported with CIs as a descriptive quantity and carries no prediction. P6 (governance cost, G9): on the clean three-writer mixed store the D0 gate flags < 10% of clean foreign items (>= 1500 items, half-width about 1.5) and costs < 3 net points vs the ungated mixed store for the Qwen3 reader (4 seeds, (game, seed)-paired half-width about +-3). Name: coverage_not_headcount
Title: Coverage, Not Headcount: What a Population of Writers Adds to an Agent's Experience Store at Matched Collection Cost
Short Hypothesis: At a fixed total collection budget, an experience store written by several policies is worth more to a reader than the reader's own store only by the task-type coverage the other writers add (types on which some writer succeeds more often than the reader), a statistic computable from the writers' collection logs before any reading. Once coverage, budget and per-type item counts are held fixed by construction, the number of writers (2 vs 8), the class of their diversity (scaffold/temperature variants of the reader's backbone vs other backbones) and the retrieval-time conflict among their items each move the reader's gain by less than the Gate-0 effect of 6 net, whereas a coverage change at the same budget and headcount moves it by at least that much; displacing half of the reader's own budget by a writer it dominates on every type costs nothing.
Related Work: Memory Sharing (2404.09982) and Multi-Agent Transactive Memory (2606.19911) show that pooling contributions from several agents helps a reader, but pool at unmatched cost, do not vary the number or kind of contributing policies, and never compare against a pool the reader collected itself with the same episodes. 'Scaling Teams or Scaling Time' (2604.03295) reports non-monotonic scaling with team size when experience is reused, as a conceptual view with one backbone and no matched-budget stores; 'Understanding Agent Scaling via Diversity' (2602.03794) bounds inference-time ensembles by the number of complementary channels, not stored experience. StateFuse (2607.05844) preserves conflicts among replicas but does not measure how store value changes with writer count or diversity. In the imitation-learning home literature, demonstration compatibility across multiple human demonstrators (2210.08073) predicts multi-demonstrator IL success for a trained policy, not for an in-context reader at matched budget. The archived contributor_conflict_not_size claimed cross-contributor conflict degrades shared libraries with conflict a property of its construction; here conflict is manipulated at fixed coverage and headcount and coverage is the pre-read predictor. The archived closer_beats_stronger claimed policy proximity, not capability, predicts transfer; here a far-but-covering writer and a near-but-dominated writer are the two arms that decide between proximity and coverage.
Abstract: Shared experience stores are now written by several agents, but their value is reported at unmatched cost, with one kind of writer, and never against the pool a reader could have collected itself with the same episodes. We ask what a population of writers adds at a fixed collection budget B and propose that the answer is a statistic computable from the writers' collection logs before any reading: the coverage complement C, the validation-weighted excess of the best writer's per-type success over the reader's own. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B and gpt-oss-120b as writers and readers, and scaffold and temperature variants of Qwen3-32B as proximity manipulations at fixed capability, we manipulate coverage, headcount, diversity class and retrieval conflict separately at the same budget: a two-writer store that adds coverage is compared with a two-writer store of identical item count that adds none; an eight-writer store is built to have exactly the coverage complement and per-type item counts of the two-writer store; four-writer stores of identical coverage differ only in whether their extra writers are proximity or capability variants; and eight-writer stores of identical coverage are filtered to one procedure skeleton per type or spread across skeletons. Every store is read with the same retriever at k=3 and reported per writer x reader cell as the retained-gain ratio against the reader's own matched-cost pool, net of a static procedure prompt, with a planted-harm positive control establishing that the pipeline detects a Gate-0 loss. We predict that a coverage change at fixed headcount moves gain by at least 6 net, that headcount, diversity class and conflict at fixed coverage each move it by less than 6 (two one-sided tests at 8 seeds), that displacing half the reader's budget by a writer it dominates on every type costs nothing, that model writers recover at least 60% of the expert writer's contribution at matched item count, and, secondarily, that C rank-correlates with gain across 21 store x reader cells.
Experiments:
- Writers and pools. B = 3,553 train episodes (the on-disk Qwen3-32B ReAct self pool, 1,892 successes). Each additional writer collects B/2 episodes on a random half of the train games (disjoint halves for pairs; the eighths used for N=8 are nested inside the halves), success-filtered, same trajectory format: Qwen3-32B plan-then-act; Qwen3-32B ReAct at T=0.7; Qwen3-32B ReAct with a self-check turn; Qwen3-32B ReAct at T=1.2 (the pre-registered dominated writer); EXAONE-4.0-32B ReAct and gpt-oss-120b ReAct at the full B (they are also those readers' self pools; halves reused); gpt-oss-120b plan-then-act at B/2 (eighth writer). Expert walkthroughs (1,465 items, no episode cost) are an item-matched writer reported separately. Per-writer per-type success profiles s_w(t) are logged at collection. Collection: 4 x 1,777 + 3,553 + 3,553 + 1,777 = 15,991 episodes.
- Predictor. Coverage complement C(S,R) = sum_t w_t * max(0, max_{w in S with items retained on t} s_w(t) - s_R(t)), w_t the validation type share; computed from collection logs and frozen, together with every store's composition, before the first evaluation cell.
- Stores at matched budget B (Qwen3-32B reader unless noted). SELF = self(B). DOM = self(B/2)+dominated(B/2): T=1.2 if s_w(t) <= s_self(t) on all six types; if it exceeds self on a type, its items on that type are dropped and the store is per-type item-count-equalized to SELF, so C(DOM) = 0 by construction. COV = self(B/2)+gpt-oss(B/2). Pairs self(B/2)+X(B/2) for X in {EXAONE, plan-then-act, T=0.7, self-check}. HCM (HET-cap-model, N=3) = {Qwen3 ReAct, EXAONE, gpt-oss} at B/3 each (capability and family varied at fixed ReAct scaffold; no expert). HCM-item = HCM subsampled per type to the expert bank's per-type item counts (item-matched; P4 numerator). HCE (N=4) = HCM writers plus the expert item-matched at a quarter share (the earlier HET-cap; secondary cell). HP4 (HET-prox, N=4) = four Qwen3-32B variants at B/4 (proximity varied at fixed capability). ALL8 = all eight model writers at B/8. EC8 (equal-coverage N=8) = the same eight writers at B/8, with the six writers other than self and gpt-oss retaining items only on types t where s_w(t) <= max(s_self(t), s_gptoss(t)), then per-type item-count-equalized to COV (symmetric: COV is subsampled if EC8 is short on a type), so C(EC8) = C(COV) and per-type counts are identical while N rises from 2 to 8. - Reading. Same retriever and injection as Measurement A, k=3 for every cell; readers Qwen3-32B (all stores above), EXAONE-4.0-32B (self_EX(B), self_EX(B/2)+Qwen3(B/2), self_EX(B/2)+gpt-oss(B/2), HCM, ALL8) and gpt-oss-120b (self_go(B), self_go(B/2)+Qwen3(B/2), HCM). 274 validation games (seen+unseen).
- Cells and episodes (274 games; 2/4/8 seeds = 548/1,096/2,192 episodes). Qwen3-32B reader: 8 seeds SELF, DOM, COV, EC8 (8,768); 4 seeds static-procedure, self(B/2) alone, HCM, HCM-item, expert-only, EC4-prox, EC4-cap, EC8-skel1, EC8-skelV, HARM (10,960); 2 seeds k=0, the four pairs, HCE, HP4, ALL8 (4,384): 24,112. EXAONE reader: 4 seeds self_EX(B), HCM; 2 seeds k=0, static, two pairs, ALL8: 4,932. gpt-oss reader: 4 seeds self_go(B), HCM; 2 seeds k=0, static, one pair: 3,836. Evaluation total 32,880 episodes; with collection 48,871.
- Outcomes per cell. Net success vs k=0; gain net of the static-procedure prompt (Measurement C); retained-gain ratio gain_R(S)/gain_R(self_R(B)) and, for backbone writers, gain_R(S)/gain_w(S), with CIs; per-type gains; retrieval-time conflict rate (fraction of top-3 sets containing >= 2 distinct skeletons for the type); below-self share (fraction of retrieved items from writers with s_w(t) < s_R(t)); injected tokens.
- Analysis. Primary: the paired contrasts of P1-P5. Secondary (P6): Spearman rho of gain-over-own-pool with frozen C across the 21 store x reader cells that contain a foreign writer, partial correlations of N, diversity class and conflict rate with C controlled, cluster-bootstrap CIs; per-type decomposition of the COV and HCM gains.
- Schedule. GPU0 serves the reader under evaluation while GPU1 collects the next writer's pool or serves the second reader. At the rate assumed for the on-disk pool (about 20 episodes/min per A100 for 32B models, about 10/min for gpt-oss-120b; re-measured in the first hour): collection 10,661 32B episodes (9 GPU-h) + 5,330 gpt-oss episodes (9 GPU-h); evaluation 29,044 32B episodes (24 GPU-h) + 3,836 gpt-oss episodes (6.4 GPU-h); about 49 GPU-h, 25 h with both A100s busy, at most 4 days with model swaps, the seed rule (<= 4,400 episodes) and a 2x throughput margin. If measured throughput is below 10 episodes/min, the 2-seed cells of the EXAONE and gpt-oss readers are cut first, then HCE; the 8-seed headline cells, HARM and self(B/2) are never cut.

- Static-procedure prompt (Measurement C), per type, every reader; every transfer gain is reported net of it.
- self_R(B) at k=3 for every reader (matched-cost self-pool control) and self(B/2) alone (what displacing half the budget costs before any writer is added; the saturation gate for P3).

Name: one_bad_apple_population_vote
Title: One Bad Apple in the Top-k: Contamination Geometry of a Population Store and the Cross-Writer Vote That Detects It
Short Hypothesis: A benign-looking wrong record (a success-formatted trajectory with a wrong procedure, or a failed trajectory relabelled as a success) planted in a multi-writer experience store harms a reader by whether it is present among the retrieved items at all rather than by its share of them: one wrong item among three costs most of the harm of three, one wrong item among seven costs most of the harm of one alone, and under natural retrieval harm tracks the logged chance that a wrong item is present rather than its mean share, so dilution by benign writers recovers only what it removes from the top-k. The only reader-side signal that scales with the population is disagreement of the item's procedure skeleton with same-type items written by other, independent writers, whose recall rises with the number of independent benign writers and is not beaten by the reader's own critique of the item; provenance exclusion is blind to poison carrying a trusted label and is costed on legitimate reuse.
Related Work: MemoryGraft (2512.16962) shows implanted 'successful experiences' drive persistent drift on one backbone and one framework, without harm-vs-rate curves or defenses. The Compliance Trap (2607.10608) diagnoses where a conflicting retrieved memory first changes an action and that early adoption compounds, but with single-writer memory and no manufactured, gated contamination or detector. In the RAG-poisoning home literature, PoisonedRAG-style attacks and defenses (TrustRAG 2501.00879 clusters retrieved passages to isolate poison; TriShieldRAG 2607.23838 adds provenance-weighted scoring and cross-LLM consensus) operate on factual QA passages with consensus across models at generation time, not across independent writers of agent trajectories, and never score recall as a function of how many writers cover a topic. Souly et al. (2510.07192) find pretraining poisoning depends on the absolute number of poison documents rather than their fraction; this proposal tests the retrieval-time analogue, presence-in-top-k versus share, including a single wrong item among seven retrieved. MAP-Graph (2608.10509) and the archived lineage_blast_radius rely on provenance labels, which by construction cannot see poison carrying a trusted label; here provenance exclusion is only costed on legitimate reuse.
Abstract: A store written by several agents can carry a wrong record that looks like a success: a fluent trajectory with the wrong procedure, or a failed trajectory relabelled as won. We manufacture both on ALFWorld's procedure-bound task types (heat, clean, cool), plant them under two carrier identities (the reader's own backbone, a foreign backbone) in a population store written by Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B, gpt-oss-120b and expert walkthroughs, and measure harm to two readers along three geometries: the retrieved share controlled directly (1/3, 2/3, 1 of the top-3); exactly one wrong item forced into the top-k at k = 1, 3, 7 (share 1 -> 1/7); and natural retrieval with 1, 2 or 4 benign writers covering the type at a fixed number of planted items, with every retrieval logged so each cell's exposure rate (games with a wrong item present) and mean poison share are measured. The central claim is that harm follows presence rather than share: removing two of three wrong items recovers little, one wrong item among seven costs nearly what one alone costs, and the dilution cells' harm equals the share-1 harm times the exposure rate, not times the share. What the population uniquely provides is a vote: an item whose procedure skeleton disagrees with same-type items written by other, independent writers is flagged, and we predict this detector's recall rises with the number of independent writers and is not beaten by the reader's own critique of the item. Detectors are scored by precision and recall against the planted labels before any downstream number; the vote is then run downstream at share 1/3 and costed in tokens against the reader-critique detector, and provenance exclusion, blind to poison carrying a trusted label, is costed on legitimate reuse. Every boundary is a fraction of the share-1 harm measured in the same run, which must reach 24 net at 8 seeds before the geometry arms are scored; a positive-control poison is the pre-registered fallback.
Experiments:
- Clean population store P: Qwen3-32B self pool, EXAONE-4.0-32B pool, gpt-oss-120b pool (B/2 episodes each; shared with coverage_not_headcount if run, else collected here at ~1.5-4 GPU-h per writer on the second GPU while the first serves the reader), expert walkthroughs; provenance tags on every item; same retriever and injection as Measurement A. Every retrieval is logged per game (top-m ids, writer, rank, planted flag), so each cell's exposure rate e (fraction of games with >= 1 planted item in the top-k) and mean planted share s are measured, not assumed.
- Poison manufacture on heat/clean/cool (Measurement A gains +39..+55 there): (a) procedure grafts: successful trajectories of a given writer with the procedure step swapped or deleted (microwave<->fridge, sink step removed), navigation and object-location content untouched; (b) relabelled failures: the writer's own failed train trajectories of the type with the outcome label set to success (Qwen3 has 1,661 failed train games); (c) positive control: the same count of items carrying an explicit wrong instruction line. Carrier identity in {self (Qwen3-written), foreign (EXAONE-written)}, graft content held fixed across carriers so only style varies. Planted lists frozen and pre-registered: n_p per target type equal to the Qwen3 pool's count of successful items of that type (target 60 per type, 180 per carrier), so the 1-writer natural share is about 0.5. Poison items length-matched to the items they replace.
- Gate 0 (feasibility gate, not a prediction): a kind proceeds if its harm at share 1 (all top-3 items poisoned, k=3, Qwen3 reader) is >= 6 net on target-type games vs the clean store. Ratio precondition: the geometry and detector arms are scored only when the share-1 harm h of the kind they use is >= 24 net at 8 seeds; they use the most harmful benign-looking kind, and if none reaches 24 they use the positive control (pre-registered fallback) and the benign-looking result is reported as the G13 answer.
- Share geometry at k=3: controlled retrieved share in {1/3, 2/3, 1} by deterministic mixing of the nearest planted items into the top-3, poison positions randomized per game.
- Count-fixed k geometry: exactly one planted item forced into the top-k at k in {1, 3, 7} (share 1, 1/3, 1/7), the clean store at the same k as the paired reference; the k=3 cell is the share-1/3 cell.
- Dilution by writers (natural retrieval, n_p fixed): benign writers covering the target types 1 -> 2 -> 4 (Qwen3 alone; +EXAONE; +gpt-oss and expert), expected share 0.5 -> 0.33 -> 0.2, e and s logged per cell.
- Detectors, scored by precision and recall against planted labels (unit: planted item, n = 180 per carrier; also per retrieval occurrence) before any downstream number: D1 cross-writer skeleton vote (retrieve m=8, parse each item to a procedure skeleton with the programmatic ALFWorld action parser, flag an item whose skeleton disagrees with the majority of same-type items from writers other than its own), run with 1, 2 and 3 other writers in the vote pool; D1-self (same m, pool restricted to the item's own writer); D3 reader LLM critique of each retrieved item ('is this a correct way to do the task?', ~500 tokens per item), in-context and memory-absent; D4 provenance exclusion of the lowest-collection-success writer (blind to poison under a trusted label; costed on the clean store only). Downstream: flagged items replaced by the next unflagged item in rank order, run at share 1/3 (one planted item in the top-3, so recovery is bounded by recall under either geometry) for D1 and D3.
- Readers: Qwen3-32B (all cells); EXAONE-4.0-32B (clean, k=0, grafts at share 2/3 with EXAONE-written and Qwen3-written carriers), so the carrier x reader crossing varies proximity at fixed carrier capability.
- Budget (target-type games ~110; 8 seeds = 880 paired episodes per cell). Qwen3 reader, 16 cells at 8 seeds: clean k=3; graft share 1, 2/3, 1/3; positive control share 1; relabelled share 1; clean and one-item at k=1; clean and one-item at k=7; dilution 1/2/4 writers; D1 and D3 downstream at share 1/3; EXAONE-carrier grafts share 2/3 = 14,080. Qwen3 reader, 4 cells at 4 seeds: k=0; static-procedure prompt; token-matched placebo; D4 on clean = 1,760. Specificity: look-at-in-light games, clean vs planted, 8 seeds, ~720. EXAONE reader: clean k=3, EXAONE-carrier 2/3, Qwen3-carrier 2/3 at 8 seeds and k=0 at 4 seeds = 3,080. Total ~19,600 episodes plus ~7,000 items x 2 variants x ~500 tokens of offline D3 critique. At the ~7,000 episodes/day of the earlier estimate this is about 3 days, about 3.5 with the heavier k=7 and D3 cells, on two A100s (one serving the reader, the other collecting pools, then serving the second reader and D3), plus at most one day under the add-seeds cap.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Clean store P at k=1/3/7, k=0 and the static-procedure prompt (Measurement C) as the floor: harm is reported relative to the clean store at the same k, and clean-store gain relative to the static prompt, for both readers (EXAONE's clean gain also as a retained-gain ratio against Qwen3's gain from the same store). No transfer benefit is claimed, so no self-pool-at-matched-cost arm is required.
- Positive control (explicit wrong instruction, share 1, 8 seeds) run before any benign-looking kind and held as the pre-registered fallback poison for the geometry arms.
- Token-matched placebo: the same number of benign items from the same writer replacing the poison at the same positions (rules out item-count and position effects).
- Specificity control: grafts planted on look-at-in-light, where memory gain is about zero, expected harmless.
- D1 with m in {5,8,12} and with 1/2/3 other writers in the pool (offline on the retrieval logs, no episodes); skeleton parser accuracy on 100 hand-labelled items; D3 in-context vs memory-absent; D3 and D1 token cost per episode reported side by side.
- Provenance exclusion D4 on the clean store: net points lost on legitimate reuse, reported next to detector token costs.
Falsifiable Predictions:
Decision rule for every prediction: the named contrast is estimated by a joint bootstrap over games with seeds as blocks; the prediction is falsified when the 95% CI lies entirely on the falsifying side of the boundary and confirmed when it lies entirely on the predicted side; a straddling CI triggers the add-seeds rule (cap 12) and is otherwise reported inconclusive. h is the share-1 harm of the poison kind used, measured in the same run (precondition h >= 24 net at 8 seeds); each prediction names the falsifying world and its distance from the boundary at h = 24.
- P1 (grafts destroy the gain). Contrast: harm(grafts, share 1) / gain(clean P vs k=0) on heat/clean/cool, Qwen3 reader, k=3. Boundary 0.5; predicted >= 0.5. Falsifying world: the reader keeps most of the gain from the graft's untouched navigation and object-location content and takes the procedure from its prior, ratio <= 0.3 (with gain ~45 and harm and gain each +/-6.5, the ratio CI is about +/-0.15, so 0.3 is more than one CI from the boundary). Arm: graft share 1 vs clean vs k=0, 8 seeds. Gate 0 (>= 6 net) is a separate feasibility gate and is not a prediction.
- P2 (one bad apple; headline). Contrast D2 = harm(share 1) - harm(share 1/3) at k=3, the recovery from removing two of three wrong items, a directly paired difference between two poisoned arms (+/-6.5). Boundary 0.35 h; predicted D2 <= 0.35 h (presence gives D2 near 0). Falsifying world: harm proportional to share, D2 = 0.67 h (16 net at h = 24, more than one CI above the 8.4-net boundary); a majority-following reader gives D2 = h. Arm: share 1 vs 1/3 at k=3 (share 2/3 reported as the middle point), positions randomized, 8 seeds.
- P3 (one bad apple survives k). Contrast D3k = harm(one item at k=1) - harm(one item at k=7), each harm against the clean store at its own k (double difference, +/-9). Boundary 0.4 h1 with h1 = harm(one item at k=1); predicted D3k <= 0.4 h1. Falsifying world: harm follows share, one item among seven costs h1/7 and D3k = 0.86 h1 (about 21 net at h1 = 24, more than one CI above the 9.6-net boundary); a majority-following reader produces it. Arm: k in {1,3,7}, one forced item, clean at the same k, 8 seeds; k=3 reported as the middle point.
- P4 (dilution acts only through exposure). Contrast X = mean over the 1/2/4-writer cells of [harm_cell - h x s_cell], the pooled excess of harm over the share model, with s_cell each cell's logged mean planted share (about 0.5/0.33/0.2). Boundary 0.17 h; predicted X >= 0.17 h (presence model: harm_cell = h x e_cell with e = 1-(1-s)^3, giving X about 0.34 h). Falsifying world: harm = h x s_cell, X = 0 (a majority-following reader gives X about -0.06 h). X carries about +/-4 net (+/-0.17 h at h = 24), so both model values sit one CI from the 4-net boundary. Arm: dilution cells, natural retrieval, 8 seeds. Reported alongside, not scored: recovery from 1 to 4 writers as a fraction of the 1-writer cell's own harm (presence predicts about 45%, share 60%).
- P5 (relabelled failures are the lesser poison). Contrast D5 = harm(grafts, share 1) - harm(relabelled failures, share 1), paired (+/-6.5). Boundary 0.5 h; predicted D5 >= 0.5 h (skeletons of failed runs are mostly right; the reader copies procedure, not outcome). Falsifying world: the reader copies the failed run's wandering as readily as a wrong procedure, D5 near 0 (12 net below the boundary at h = 24). Arm: relabelled vs graft at share 1, 8 seeds. A relabelled harm below Gate 0 is a confirming outcome and is reported as the answer to G13's benign-record question; detector cells run on grafts regardless.
- P6 (the detector needs the population). D1 with 3 other independent writers in the vote pool reaches recall >= 0.7 at precision >= 0.7 on grafts and exceeds D1-self recall by >= 0.2; recall rises monotonically from 1 to 3 other writers with the 3-minus-1 difference >= 0.15. Falsified if D1-self is within 0.1 of D1 (one writer's redundancy suffices), if D1 recall < 0.5 (parser failure or natural skeleton variation floods the vote), or if the 1-other-writer pool already reaches the 3-writer recall within 0.05. Unit: planted items (n = 180 per carrier; Wilson CI about +/-0.07 at 0.7, +/-0.1 on a difference) and retrieval occurrences. Arm: vote-pool composition at fixed m=8, planted labels as ground truth, offline on the retrieval logs.
- P7 (a programmatic vote is enough). (a) Downstream at share 1/3: recovery = [success(D1) - success(no detector)] / harm(1/3), boundary 0.5, predicted >= 0.5 (presence with recall 0.7 gives about 0.7). Falsifying world: recovery <= 0.2 (P6 fails, or the next unflagged replacement is as often another planted item); ratio CI about +/-0.3, so 0.2 is one CI below the boundary; scored only if harm(1/3) >= 12, else reported descriptively because under a share geometry one item cannot carry measurable harm. (b) Item level, at precision >= 0.7: D1 recall minus D3 memory-absent recall on grafts, boundary -0.1, predicted >= -0.1 (the vote loses at most 0.1 recall to the LLM critique). Falsifying world: the reader's explicit critique catches the wrong procedures its acting policy copies, difference <= -0.25 (0.15 beyond the boundary at Wilson +/-0.1). Token overhead per episode (parser vs ~4,000 LLM tokens for 8 items) is reported descriptively and is not part of any falsifier. Arm: D1 vs D3 vs no detector at share 1/3, 8 seeds; item-level scoring on the same logs.
- P8 (carrier proximity at fixed content). Contrast per reader: harm(own-backbone carrier) - harm(foreign carrier) at share 2/3 with identical wrong procedures, a paired difference between two poisoned arms (+/-6.5). Boundary 8 net; predicted >= 8 for the Qwen3 reader (Qwen3-written > EXAONE-written) and for the EXAONE reader (EXAONE-written > Qwen3-written). Falsifying world: harm depends on content only, difference 0 for either reader (more than one CI below the boundary). Arm: 2 carriers x 2 readers, all four cells at 8 seeds.
Measurement and Noise Control: Harm is the paired per-game net success on target-type games (about 110 of the 274) with the clean store at the same k as the paired reference. Every claim-bearing cell runs at 8 seeds (880 paired episodes); scaling the brief's +/-8 at 274 x 2 seeds gives about +/-6.5 on a paired harm and on a paired difference between two poisoned arms that share games and seeds, and about +/-9 on a double difference across k. Add-2-seeds rule when a CI straddles a boundary, cap 12 seeds. Ratio-type contrasts (P1, P4, P7a) and every boundary expressed as a fraction of h are estimated by joint bootstrap over games with seeds as blocks, so the shared term h (which enters P2, P3, P4, P5, P7 and P8) is resampled together with the numerator. The precondition h >= 24 net, with the positive-control fallback, is what makes every band at least one CI wide; the arithmetic is given per prediction. Non-target games are the specificity control. Detector precision and recall carry Wilson CIs over planted items (n = 180 per carrier) and over retrieval occurrences, reported per poison kind and per carrier. Exposure rate e and mean share s are read from the per-game retrieval logs, never assumed. Poison positions in the top-k are randomized per game; planted-item lists are frozen and pre-registered; retriever, injection format and token counts are identical across arms except where k or a detector changes them, in which case the clean reference is matched at the same k.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The share-1 harm of benign-looking kinds may fall below the 24-net precondition (grafts keep navigation and object-location content, which may carry much of the memory gain); the geometry arms then run on the positive control and the benign-looking result is reported as the G13 answer, which weakens the 'benign-looking' framing but not the geometry claim. Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: Measurement A ('gain carried by clean/heat/cool procedures'); this idea claims that harm is carried by the same procedure-bound types and follows presence in the top-k rather than share, up to one wrong item among seven, which a clean bank cannot show. Nearest archived idea: lineage_blast_radius relied on provenance labels and was judged entailed; here labels are shown blind to labelled poison and the detector is content-based across writers; 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap) is single-writer with no dilution or vote.
Changes made:

- P5: scored as the paired difference graft minus relabelled with its own CI, boundary 0.5 h under the h >= 24 precondition; the escape clause is removed (a relabelled harm below Gate 0 is a confirming outcome; detector cells run on grafts regardless).
- P6: content unchanged; unit of analysis fixed (planted items, n = 180 per carrier, Wilson +/-0.07) and the 1/2/3-other-writer recall curve added to the prediction.
- P7: token clause dropped from the falsifier (cost reported descriptively); downstream cells moved to share 1/3 with the denominator named (harm(1/3) of the same run) and a stated dependence on P2; the D1-vs-D3 comparison moved to the item level (recall at matched precision, Wilson CIs) where it is powered, keeping the sharp claim that the population vote is not beaten by the reader's own critique.

Budget restated cell by cell (~19,600 episodes, about 3.5 days on two A100s).
