Name: reader_pays_writer_detours
Title: The Reader Pays the Writer's Detours: Consumer-Side Cost of Transferred Experience Tracks the Writer's Episode Length, Not Its Success
Short Hypothesis: The consumer-side cost of using a foreign experience pool (served tokens, generated and observation tokens and steps per episode) is inherited from the writer's trajectory length: a reader copies the step structure of the retrieved item, so on-policy self pools (long, with detours) cost more per successful episode than minimal expert walkthroughs at equal success. Pruning replay-verified detours from self items at fixed content removes the inherited cost without losing success, and padding expert walkthroughs with benign detours adds it; consequently the ranking of writers by gain per consumer token differs from their ranking by success, and cost-matched comparisons across writers must charge the reader's served tokens, not only the injected ones.
Related Work: Consumer-side inference tokens are not reported with transfer gains (digest gap G22): AMD (arxiv:2608.07169) omits student-side overhead, SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) compares raw trajectories and skills without matched per-reader token cost, memory-system profiling (arxiv:2606.24775) attributes cost to phases for a single writer, PAST-Bench (arxiv:2608.04003) and S3Gym (arxiv:2608.31100) report gains without the retention cost. AgentDiet (arxiv:2509.23586) reduces the agent's own context history to cut cost and inference-time distillation (arxiv:2512.02543) moves the ALFWorld cost-accuracy frontier with teacher demonstrations, but neither asks whether the reader's episode length depends on the retrieved item's length. MemoryCPT (arxiv:2608.04843) optimizes quality per inference cost within one writer-reader pair. In the home literature, Extraneousness-Aware Imitation Learning (arxiv:2210.01379) filters irrelevant segments from noisy demonstrations to recover performance, and 'What Demonstration Curation Metrics Do to Your Policy' (arxiv:2606.10229) shows defect detection and downstream policy quality decouple; both concern success, not inherited episode cost, and neither swaps the demonstrator. The archived idea abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied abstraction level within one writer on the success axis; here length is manipulated at fixed content with writer identity swapped and the outcome is the reader's cost.
Abstract: Transfer results report what the reader gains, not what the reader pays. We propose that the consumer-side cost of transferred experience is set by the writer's path length: LLM readers imitate the step structure of retrieved items, so a self pool of on-policy successes (which contain failed actions, 'Nothing happens' observations and revisits) makes the reader's own episodes longer than an expert walkthrough does, even when success is equal. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B as readers, the writer set is expert walkthroughs, Qwen3's own k=0 successes and EXAONE's own k=0 successes, all rendered in one action-observation format by environment replay and retrieved by one retriever whose ordering is fixed on the unmanipulated pools. Two content-preserving manipulations, applied to the retrieved items after retrieval and replay-verified, vary length at fixed content with a controlled dose: expert-padded inserts d benign detour steps (d drawn uniformly from 0 to 14 per game and seed, sampled from the self pool's detour distribution), and self-pruned removes every step whose replayed state diff is empty. A third arm, expert-corrupted, inserts detours that make the replayed walkthrough fail and is the positive control that the cells detect content damage. The manipulation cells run at 4 seeds (1,096 paired episodes per pair); we estimate the length-inheritance slope of the within-game, within-seed change in reader steps on the change in mean retrieved-item steps over all episodes with step-cap censoring modeled, and report success, steps, served tokens (all prompt and completion tokens the reader's replica processes per episode) and gain per 1k served tokens per writer x reader cell, net of k=0 and of the static3 prompt (Measurement C), together with the retained-gain ratio. Predictions: a slope of at least 0.3 in both manipulation pairs and for the foreign reader (expected SE 0.07 to 0.12, so a true slope near zero yields a CI upper bound below 0.3); pruning and padding within 6 net of their unmanipulated versions at a paired MDE of about 5.3 net; and a writer ranking by gain per served token that differs from the ranking by success, with the ratio's CI. The result gives transfer evaluation a cost axis on the reader's side and a cheap, replay-verified pruning step that any writer's pool can pass through before sharing.
Experiments: Preparation (CPU env replay, about half a day): render all pools into one action-observation item format by replaying the writer's actions; label every item step by its replayed state diff (empty diff, including 'Nothing happens' actions and revisits without change, = detour); build self-pruned (all empty-diff steps removed, replay-verified to still complete the task; items failing replay dropped and counted by writer); at read time build expert-padded (d detour steps, d uniform on 0..14 drawn per game and seed, sampled from the self pool's detour distribution and inserted at random positions between walkthrough actions, replay-verified) and expert-corrupted (every retrieved item receives d uniform on 1..14 state-changing detours, a take/put pair that relocates the task object, so the replayed walkthrough fails). Retrieval ordering is computed once on the unmanipulated pools and reused in every cell, so a manipulation changes only the injected items' content and length. Item lengths are logged (mean steps: expert, self-raw, self-pruned, expert-padded by dose, EXAONE-raw, EXAONE-pruned). Collection: EXAONE k=0 pool on the 3,553 train games (about 3 GPU-hours) on one A100 while the other serves the Qwen3 reader cells; each self pool is one k=0 pass per backbone over the same games, so foreign and self pools share the collection budget. Reader cells on the 274 eval games: 548 episodes per 2 seeds (about 30 min per replica), 1,096 per 4 seeds. Qwen3 reader at k=3, 4 seeds: expert (replayed), expert-padded, self-raw, self-pruned, expert-corrupted (5 x 1,096 = 5,480). Qwen3 reader at k=3, 2 seeds: EXAONE-raw, EXAONE-pruned, k=0 (2 seeds added to Measurement C's 2), static3 (2 seeds added), self-raw in the writer's native rendering (format control), expert-padded with observation text truncated to the unpadded item's token count and self-raw with observation text truncated to the pruned item's token count (token-matched length controls) (7 x 548 = 3,836). EXAONE reader at k=3, 4 seeds: Qwen3-raw, Qwen3-pruned, own-raw, own-pruned (4 x 1,096 = 4,384). EXAONE reader at k=3, 2 seeds: expert, k=0, static3 (3 x 548 = 1,644). Total 19 cells, 15,344 episodes, about 14 replica-hours plus the 3-hour collection, about 8.5 wall-hours on two A100s; the pre-registered contingency (2 more seeds on up to eight manipulation and neutrality cells, 4,384 episodes, about 4 replica-hours) keeps the study under 2 days. Per episode we log success, steps, generated tokens, observation tokens, injected tokens, prompt tokens per request (summed as served tokens), the retrieved items' ids, doses and step counts, and whether the step cap was hit. Analyses: (i) paired success differences per cell with bootstrap CIs over games, stratified by type; (ii) reader steps and served tokens per episode, all episodes with right-censoring at the step cap (Tobit) and successful-only; (iii) the length-inheritance slope per manipulation pair and reader: within-game, within-seed change in reader steps regressed on the change in mean retrieved-item steps, Tobit at the cap as primary and OLS on jointly successful episodes as secondary; (iv) gain per 1k served tokens with bootstrap CIs, and the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell (reader's gain from the writer's pool over the writer's own gain from the same pool, and over the reader's self-pool gain), in success and per served token; (v) the pruning rule scored by precision and recall of its step removals against the replayed state-diff labels.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 (4 seeds for the Qwen3 reader, 2 for EXAONE); static3, the best static-procedure prompt of Measurement C (3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, about 430 tokens), at 4 seeds for Qwen3 and 2 for EXAONE, every gain reported net of it; the wrong-type placebo blind1 reused from Measurement C (paired on the same games and seeds, no rerun); self-pool control at matched collection cost (each reader's own k=0 pass over the same 3,553 train games as the foreign pool); retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell with CIs; expert-corrupted as the manufactured, positively controlled contamination arm (Gate 0: its harm must be at least 6 net for the neutrality cells to count as sensitive); token-matched length controls (padded items with observation text truncated to the unpadded token count; raw self items truncated to the pruned token count) to separate item steps from item tokens, which also compares the adaptation step (pruning) with direct injection of the unmodified item at matched tokens; native-rendering control for the self pool (writer's own reasoning text kept, item steps unchanged) to show format does not carry the length effect; the k=3 vs k=7 injected-token difference of Measurement C (430 vs 1,010 tokens) as the accounting positive control. Cut from the previous version because they carried no prediction: the k=1 cells, random-deletion pruning (replaced by the state-diff labels and by the padding pair, which varies length in the opposite direction with content held fixed) and the own-vs-other detour-source padding.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline, length inheritance): for the Qwen3 reader at k=3, in each manipulation pair (expert vs expert-padded, dose 0..14; self-raw vs self-pruned), the within-game, within-seed change in reader steps regressed on the change in mean retrieved-item steps over all 1,096 paired episodes (Tobit at the step cap) has a slope of at least 0.3 with a 95% CI lower bound above 0.1. Falsifier: the slope's 95% CI upper bound is below 0.3 in either pair (the reader plans from the item rather than copying its path). Reachable: with 1,096 pairs, a residual SD of about 10 steps and an item-step-change SD of 4.3 (padding) or about 2.5 (pruning, pilot-estimated), the SE is about 0.07 and 0.12, so a true slope of 0 gives an upper bound of about 0.14 and 0.24, and a true slope of 0.1 is rejected in the padding pair with power about 0.8; the achieved SE is reported and the contingency seeds are pre-registered. Arm: the four manipulation cells at 4 seeds; injected tokens rise with padding by construction and are excluded from this estimand. P2 (pruning is success-neutral): in both readers at 4 seeds, self-pruned minus self-raw lies within 6 net with the 90% CI inside [-6, +6] (paired MDE about 5.3 net). Falsifier: pruned at least 6 net below raw with the 95% CI excluding 0, the outcome the cue-discarding account of arxiv:2605.24117 predicts; arm: the pruned vs raw cells (Qwen3 own pair, EXAONE own pair). P3 (padding is success-neutral, gated): expert-padded minus expert lies within 6 net (90% CI inside [-6, +6]) while expert-corrupted is at least 6 net below expert (the positive control). Falsifier: padded at least 6 net below expert with CI excluding 0 (detours contaminate content, not only cost); if the corrupted arm fails to reach 6 net harm the cell is declared insensitive and P3 is reported as untested, not confirmed; arm: expert-padded, expert-corrupted and expert cells. P4 (cost reranks writers): for the Qwen3 reader, gain per 1k served tokens (net success over k=0 divided by mean served tokens per episode, bootstrap CI over games) of the expert pool exceeds that of self-raw by at least 25% with the ratio's 95% CI lower bound above 1.0, while the paired success gains of the two pools are within 8 net. Falsifier: the ratio's CI upper bound is at most 1.0 (self-raw's gain per served token is at least the expert's), or the success gap is at least 8 net with CI excluding 0 so that the cost ranking merely follows success; arm: expert vs self-raw cells at 4 seeds with token accounting. P5 (foreign reader inherits, no self-recognition): EXAONE reading Qwen3-raw vs Qwen3-pruned at 4 seeds (same estimand and count as P1) shows a slope of at least 0.3, and within the EXAONE reader the slope on its own pair (own-raw vs own-pruned, 4 seeds) minus the slope on the Qwen3 pair has a 95% CI that includes 0 (SE of the difference about 0.17). Falsifiers, each with its own CI and neither conditional on P1's outcome: (a) the Qwen3-pair slope's CI upper bound is below 0.3; (b) the own-minus-foreign slope difference is at least 0.2 with its CI excluding 0 (inheritance is partly self-recognition); arm: the four EXAONE 4-seed cells; the Qwen3 reader's EXAONE-raw vs EXAONE-pruned pair at 2 seeds is reported as a wider-CI replication. None is entailed: the reader may ignore item structure (P1, P5), detours may carry object-location cues (P2), inserted detours may mislead (P3), and cost may simply track success (P4); P4's token gap is partly produced by P1's slope, but P4 fails independently whenever self-raw's success gain exceeds the expert's by 8 net or its per-token ratio is not above 1.
Measurement and Noise Control: All cells are paired on the same 274 games with the same retrieval ordering; bootstrap over games, stratified by type. Success: Measurement C's paired CI half-width at 274 x 2 seeds is about 5.25 net (SE 2.7), the 8-net floor of the brief; the neutrality cells run at 4 seeds, where episode-level noise halves in variance (SE about 1.9, half-width 3.7, MDE about 5.3 net at 80% power), so the 6-net margin is above the resolvable MDE; the achieved SE is computed from the data and, if the achieved MDE exceeds 6 net, the neutrality cells get 2 more seeds from the contingency rather than the margin being reported as met. Cross-writer success differences keep the 8-net margin. Slope: the estimand is the within-game, within-seed paired difference, so eval-game difficulty cancels; the dose design (d uniform on 0..14, drawn per game and seed) makes the item-step change vary within game across seeds; expected SE 0.07 (padding) and 0.12 (pruning) at 1,096 pairs, from residual SD about 10 steps (all episodes) and item-step-change SD 4.3 and 2.5; after the first 2 seeds the achieved SDs are used to project the 4-seed SE and, if it exceeds 0.08 (padding) or 0.14 (pruning), the manipulation cells extend to 6 seeds within the contingency budget. Censoring: reader steps are right-censored at the run's step cap; the slope is estimated by Tobit on all episodes (primary) and by OLS on jointly successful episodes (secondary), and the censoring fraction per cell is reported. Cost: served tokens are the sum of prompt and completion tokens over all requests in an episode from the vLLM usage fields; generated, observation and injected tokens are also summed per episode, and injected tokens are reported separately so the by-construction part of any cost change is visible. Order: k=0, static3 and the unmanipulated writers first; manipulation cells only after the replayed expert cell reproduces Measurement C's k3 within 8 net (k3 minus static3 = +17.2, CI about +/-5). Throughput and queue occupancy per replica are logged; the EXAONE collection overlaps the Qwen3 reader cells so both A100s stay busy.

Q6 (closest named method, channel: s2cli S2+HF, hits from hf): 'raw trajectory reuse versus distilled skills inference token cost per-episode compute agent memory' -> SkillEvolBench 2605.24117 (raw beats skills, no per-reader token matching), MemoryCPT 2608.04843 (cost-aware memory construction, single writer), Evidence Over Plans 2605.09192 (efficient skills, low inference cost), 2605.12978 (consolidated memories become faulty), Activity Frames 2608.05784, AgentDiet. No preprint found that reports a length-inheritance effect from retrieved experience or a writer ranking by gain per consumer token.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Replay verification requires deterministic ALFWorld replays; items that fail replay are dropped and the drop rate by writer and manipulation is reported (a high rate would bias the pruned pool toward simpler items, checked by comparing type and length distributions). The pruning rule uses replayed state diffs, but a detour with an empty state diff can still carry an object-location cue; P2 tests that directly and the padding pair varies length in the other direction. The step cap censors long episodes; the Tobit estimate assumes a latent normal step count and is reported alongside the successful-only estimate. Item tokens and item steps co-vary; the token-matched controls truncate observation text, which is itself a manipulation, and are reported as controls, not as primary cells. The pruning-pair lever (item-step-change SD about 2.5) is weaker than the padding lever, so its slope has a wider CI; the contingency seeds are budgeted for it. The retained-gain ratio has a wide CI when the writer's own gain is small. EXAONE serving is unverified (fallback gpt-oss-120b, which changes the foreign-reader cells' cost but not the design). No proximity claim is made: P5 predicts the absence of a self-recognition effect on the slope, so the capability-versus-proximity separation of the brief is not invoked. Only ALFWorld is used; in environments with cheap steps the cost consequence is small even if inheritance holds, and the reranking in P4 depends on the success gaps measured here.
Addresses gap: G22 (consumer-side inference-token and per-episode cost reported with the gain, cost-matched across writers and manipulated at fixed content).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: 'Injected tokens ~140/430/1,010 at k=1/3/7' reports only injected tokens for one writer; this idea claims the dominant consumer-side cost is generated steps inherited from the writer's path and manipulates that path at fixed content across writers. Digest card arxiv:2605.24117 finds raw trajectories beat distilled skills on success in a single-writer setting without per-reader token cost; this idea claims the raw trajectory's success advantage comes with an inherited cost that pruning removes without losing success, with writer identity swapped. Archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs varied abstraction level within one writer on the success axis; pruning and padding are not abstraction (content is held fixed and replay-verified), the outcome is the reader's cost, and the writer is manipulated.
Changes made: P1: manipulation-pair cells raised from 2 to 4 seeds (1,096 paired episodes per pair); padding given a per-game, per-seed dose (0..14 detour steps) so the item-step change varies within game and the lever SD is 4.3; primary slope estimated on all episodes with step-cap censoring modeled (Tobit), successful-only as secondary, so cap-hitting detour-copying episodes are kept; falsifier restated as the CI upper bound below the claimed 0.3 (a true zero slope reaches it at SE 0.07 to 0.12), with the SE arithmetic stated and a pre-registered contingency to 6 seeds. P2 and P3: neutrality cells at 4 seeds so the paired MDE (about 5.3 net) is below the 6-net margin; equivalence stated as a 90% CI inside [-6, +6]; rule added that the margin is met by evidence, not insensitivity (seeds added if the achieved MDE exceeds 6). P3: expert-corrupted arm added (replay-failing detours at the same dose) as the positive control that the cell detects content damage at the Gate-0 level; P3 gated on it. P4: cost measure changed to served tokens (all prompt and completion tokens the reader processes), bootstrap CI added to the gain-per-token ratio, confirm requires the ratio's CI lower bound above 1. P5: EXAONE manipulation pair at 4 seeds (same count as the self reader); falsifier restated as two outcomes with their own CIs (foreign-pair slope upper bound below 0.3; within-reader own-minus-foreign slope difference at least 0.2 with CI excluding 0), no longer conditional on P1. Binding rules: retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell added; self-pool control at matched collection cost stated; pruning rule scored by precision and recall against replayed state-diff labels; retrieval ordering fixed on the unmanipulated pools. Cut to fit the envelope: k=1 cells, random-deletion pruning, own-vs-other detour-source padding. Claim kept as sharp: the slope threshold (0.3), the neutrality margin (6 net, now resolvable), the 25% reranking and the foreign-reader inheritance are unchanged; the one softening refused was lowering the slope threshold to what 2 seeds could detect, answered instead with seeds and a dose design.

Name: reconstruction_pays_only_across_the_writer_gap
Title: Reconstruction Pays Only Across the Writer Gap: Reader-Side Rewriting of Foreign Experience Helps by Policy Distance, Not Writer Capability, at Matched Tokens
Short Hypothesis: Training-free read-time reconstruction (the reader rewrites the k=3 retrieved items into one plan in its own action grammar, conditioned on its first observation; the plan replaces the items) adds nothing over verbatim injection at k=7 (a comparator with at least the reconstruction arm's consumer tokens and more items) when the writer is the reader itself, and adds an increment of at least one third of the Gate-0 verbatim gain (about 6.5 net given the measured k7 - static3 = +19.5) when the writer is a different 32B backbone or the same backbone under a different action scaffold. The increment tracks writer-reader policy distance (different scaffold > temperature-only sampling from the same scaffold) and not writer capability (thinking mode under the same scaffold), survives length-matching of the banks, and is not reproduced by the same rewrite applied to the fixed static3 exemplars.
Related Work: MemHarness (2607.28272) shows critique-and-reconstruct beats verbatim replay, but the retrieved experience is the agent's own, the reconstruction policy is GRPO-trained (so the gain is not separated from training), and per-step token cost is not matched. Echo (2604.05533) adapts the agent's own Minecraft experience analogically; 2406.14596 abstracts sub-optimal demonstrations with human feedback; neither varies the writer. AdaCoM (2605.30785) finds that how much a frozen agent's context should be compressed depends on the agent's own baseline strength, but manages the agent's own trajectory, not another writer's experience, and reports no writer x reader cell. The cross-embodiment imitation literature (ImMimic 2509.10952, TrajSkill 2510.07773) translates demonstrations across a domain gap, which is the mechanism claimed here, but has no LLM-text analogue with the demonstrator manipulated at matched cost. Measurement C on this node (274 games x 2 seeds, paired with the k-sweep) gives the verbatim expert->Qwen3-32B result over the best static arm: k3 - static3 = +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4], k7 - static3 = +19.5, look-at +4.8 with CI including 0; nothing on this node has measured any adaptation step. Archived closer_beats_stronger (5.75) claimed proximity predicts raw transfer without separating it from capability and without a self-pool control; archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varies abstraction level within one writer and holds the writer fixed.
Abstract: Adaptation methods for agent memory (reconstruction, analogical adaptation, abstraction) are validated only on experience the agent wrote itself, so it is unknown whether the adaptation step is a planning aid that helps regardless of who wrote the item or a translation step whose value depends on the writer. We manipulate the writer of an ALFWorld experience bank while holding the task set, bank construction, retriever and reader fixed: expert walkthroughs; the reader's own successes at matched collection cost; the same backbone under a different action scaffold at T=0 (phrasing distance at fixed capability); the same backbone at T=0.7 under the standard scaffold (sampling distance at fixed capability and phrasing); the same backbone in thinking mode under the standard scaffold (capability at fixed phrasing); and a second 32B backbone's successes. Two readers (Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B) read both backbones' banks with the roles of own and foreign reversed. Every gain is net of Measurement C's best static arm (static3; k7 - static3 = +19.5 net for the expert bank read by Qwen3-32B). For each writer x reader cell we compare training-free reconstruction at k=3 (one rewrite at step 0 of the three items into a plan in the reader's own action grammar, which replaces the items) against verbatim injection at k=7, a comparator with at least the reconstruction arm's consumer tokens and more items, and against the same rewrite applied to static3's fixed exemplars and to items retrieved for the wrong task type. The estimands are the reconstruction increment D over verbatim k=7 per cell and the retained-gain ratio before and after reconstruction, with cluster-bootstrap CIs over 274 games x 8 seeds for every cell that enters a prediction; the margin is pre-registered as the larger of one third of the Gate-0 verbatim gain and the realized half-width of the headline difference-of-differences, so every falsifier lies outside the noise. The central claim is an interaction: D is near zero for the self-written natural-length bank and exceeds it by the margin for the cross-backbone and different-scaffold banks, ordered by policy distance (scaffold > temperature-only) and not by writer capability (thinking mode), surviving length-matching and not reproduced by the placebo. A null or reversed interaction falsifies it; the natural-length self bank, whose wandering trajectories the rewrite can compress, the temperature-only bank and the thinking-mode bank can each produce that outcome. Consumer-side tokens and episodes per minute are reported with every gain.
Experiments:
- Banks (writers). All from the 3,553 train games (the 1,465 expert walkthroughs for W_exp), success-filtered, type-balanced to the expert pool's type distribution, at natural length (no cap) in the primary cells; length-capped copies (<= 2x the expert median steps) of the two headline banks are the mechanism ablation (P8). W_exp: expert walkthroughs (on disk). W_self: Qwen3-32B standard ReAct, non-thinking, T=0 (on disk). W_scaf: Qwen3-32B non-thinking, plan-then-act scaffold with different action phrasing, T=0 (collect, ~3 GPU-h). W_temp: Qwen3-32B non-thinking, standard scaffold, T=0.7 (collect, ~3 GPU-h). W_cap: Qwen3-32B thinking mode, standard scaffold, T=0 with a 2,048-token thinking cap (collect, ~8 GPU-h; if its k=0 success at T=0 is not >= 8 net above W_self, T=0.6 is used and W_temp serves as the temperature control). W_other: EXAONE-4.0-32B standard scaffold, T=0 (collect after serving verification, ~3 GPU-h). W_big is dropped. Bank verification before any confirmatory cell (274 games x 2 seeds at k=0 under the writer's own scaffold): W_scaf and W_temp within +/-5 net of W_self (fixed capability); W_cap >= +8 net above W_self (capability moved); policy distance to R1 = Jensen-Shannon divergence between the writer's and R1's action-template distributions (verb + argument pattern) over the same games, reported per bank, with the pre-registered ordering W_self < W_temp <= W_cap < W_scaf < W_other required to hold; if W_cap's divergence exceeds W_scaf's, P3 is reported as confounded rather than re-mapped.
- Readers: R1 Qwen3-32B standard non-thinking, T=0; R2 EXAONE-4.0-32B, T=0. Same retriever as Measurement C. R1's self-pool is W_self and R2's self-pool is W_other, each collected at the same episode budget as every foreign bank.
- Conditions: C0 no memory; C_static = static3 (Measurement C's best static arm: 3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens, cached); C_v3 verbatim k=3 (equal-items comparator; on disk for W_exp->R1); C_v7 verbatim k=7 (~1,010 injected tokens per step; the primary comparator, with at least the reconstruction arm's total consumer tokens and more items); C_r3 reconstruction k=3 (one rewrite call at step 0: task + first observation + the 3 items -> a plan of <= 300 tokens in the reader's own action grammar, which replaces the items in every later step; ~1k consumer tokens for the rewrite plus <= 300 per step); C_pl_static: the same rewrite prompt applied to static3's three fixed exemplars (memory-absent placebo, no retrieval); C_pl_mis: the same rewrite prompt applied to k=3 items retrieved for a different task type (mismatched placebo; also the manufactured wrong-item arm at rate 1.0; no detector is claimed). A 40-game pilot per reader logs total consumer tokens per episode for C_r3, C_v3 and C_v7; if C_r3 exceeds C_v7, k is raised until the verbatim arm has at least C_r3's tokens, and the matched k is reported.
- Estimands: reconstruction increment D(w,r) = S(r,C_r3,w) - S(r,C_v7,w); verbatim retained-gain ratio rho_v(w,r) = [S(r,C_v7,w) - S(r,static3)] / [S(r,C_v7,selfpool(r)) - S(r,static3)] and rho_r(w,r) with C_r3 in the numerator over the same denominator (so rho_r - rho_v = D divided by the self-pool gain; rho_v(W_self,R1) = 1 by construction); all with cluster-bootstrap CIs; per-type breakdown (exploratory); consumer tokens per episode (prompt + generated, including the rewrite call) and episodes/min per cell.
- Margin: M = max(G0/3, h_DiD), where G0 = S(R1,C_v7,W_far) - S(R1,static3) for the headline foreign bank W_far and h_DiD = the realized 95% cluster-bootstrap half-width of the headline difference-of-differences at 8 seeds (expected ~5.7 net if noise scales as 1/sqrt(seeds) from the +/-8 at 2 seeds; if h_DiD > 7 the four P1 cells are extended to 12 seeds before the test). M_R2 is defined the same way from R2's Gate-0 gain S(R2,C_v7,W_self) - S(R2,static3).
- Gate 0 (before confirmatory cells): (a) W_far = W_other if S(R1,C_v7,W_other) - S(R1,static3) >= +12 net with CI excluding 0 at the first 4 of the 8 seeds; otherwise W_far = W_exp (measured +19.5, so M = 6.5) and the cross-backbone headline is reported as unsupported; (b) C_r3 on (W_exp,R1) at 2 seeds is not below C_v7 by more than the 2-seed half-width (a broken rewrite prompt shows as a large drop); (c) the pilot token match above.
- Cells (274 games each; 8 seeds = 2,192 episodes unless stated). R1: static3 (2 Measurement-C seeds reused + 6 new, 1,644), C_pl_static, C_pl_mis, {W_self, W_other, W_scaf, W_temp, W_cap, W_exp} x {C_v7, C_r3} (12 cells; W_exp C_v7 reuses its 2 seeds), {W_self^cap, W_other^cap} x {C_v7, C_r3} (4 cells; if W_far = W_exp only W_self^cap is built, since the expert bank is already at the cap): 19 cells, ~40k episodes. R2: static3, {W_self, W_other} x {C_v7, C_r3} (5 cells, ~11k), W_exp x {C_v7, C_r3} at 4 seeds (2.2k), C0 at 2 seeds (0.5k): ~13.7k. Ablations on (W_far,R1) at 4 seeds: reconstruct-every-5-steps, provenance revealed (2.2k). Bank verification k=0 runs: 3 x 548 = 1.6k. Total ~58k episodes plus ~17 GPU-h of bank collection. Throughput: ~20 episodes/min per replica for verbatim, ~12-15 for reconstruction, blended ~15/min/replica: 58k / 15 = ~64 replica-hours, plus 17 GPU-h of collection = ~81 GPU-h over two A100s = ~41 h of wall time (one A100 serves R1 throughout while the other collects the four banks and then serves R2 and the remaining R1 cells); ~2.5 days with the pilot and re-runs.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest baseline first: static3 (Measurement C) and the reconstruction placebo on static3, both before any retrieval cell.
- Primary comparator for every reconstruction cell: direct injection of the unmodified items at k=7 (C_v7), which has at least the reconstruction arm's total consumer tokens (pilot-verified; k raised if not) and more items, and which Measurement C shows is the stronger verbatim arm (+19.5 vs +17.2 over static3); C_v3 is the equal-items comparator (on disk for W_exp->R1).
- Self-pool control at matched collection cost: W_self for R1 and W_other for R2, collected at the same episode budget as every foreign bank; every foreign-bank gain and increment is reported against that cell, and rho_v, rho_r use it as the denominator.
- Placebos: C_pl_static (memory-absent), C_pl_mis (mismatched; also the manufactured wrong-item arm at rate 1.0, no detector claimed).
- Ablations: length-capped copies of the two headline banks (P8, 8 seeds); reconstruct-every-5-steps on (W_far,R1) at 4 seeds (does state-conditioning beyond step 0 add anything at its token cost); writer identity revealed vs hidden in the rewrite prompt on (W_far,R1) at 4 seeds (does the reader use provenance); thinking-mode bank at T=0.6 if the T=0 collection fails verification, with W_temp as its temperature control.
- Named reimplementation: MemHarness-style critique-and-reconstruct prompt without RL (2607.28272) as C_r3; the GRPO-trained version is out of budget and is named as the untested arm.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline interaction): D(W_far,R1) - D(W_self,R1) >= M with a 95% cluster-bootstrap CI excluding 0 (M >= h_DiD by construction, so the predicted effect lies outside the noise). Falsifier: the CI includes 0 or the point estimate is negative, i.e. reconstruction helps the reader's own natural-length bank as much as or more than the foreign bank. Arm: {W_self, W_far} x {C_v7, C_r3} for R1 at 8 seeds; the self cell can produce a large D because the natural-length self bank contains wandering on-policy trajectories that the rewrite can compress into a short plan (the length cap that would remove this route is now only the P8 ablation).
- P2 (proximity at fixed capability): D(W_scaf,R1) - D(W_self,R1) >= M with CI excluding 0. Falsifier: CI includes 0 or negative (a different action scaffold from the same backbone at the same k=0 success gains nothing from translation). Arm: {W_scaf, W_self} x {C_v7, C_r3} for R1 at 8 seeds, with W_scaf verified within +/-5 net of W_self at k=0.
- P3 (capability at fixed proximity): D(W_scaf,R1) - D(W_cap,R1) >= M with CI excluding 0 (the primary test; it does not use the W_self cell), and, as an equivalence statement, the 90% CI of D(W_cap,R1) - D(W_self,R1) lies within [-M, +M] (TOST; a CI that straddles +M is reported as inconclusive, a distinct outcome). Falsifier: D(W_scaf) - D(W_cap) has a CI including 0 or negative (the thinking-mode bank gains as much from rewriting as the different-scaffold bank: capability distance governs), or the 90% CI of D(W_cap) - D(W_self) extends beyond +M. Arm: {W_cap, W_scaf, W_self} x {C_v7, C_r3} for R1 at 8 seeds, with W_cap verified >= +8 net above W_self at k=0 and with divergence to R1 not above W_scaf's.
- P4 (format distance, not trajectory diversity): D(W_scaf,R1) - D(W_temp,R1) >= M with CI excluding 0. Falsifier: CI includes 0 or negative (the temperature-only bank, same phrasing but more diverse and longer trajectories, gains as much: the increment tracks what rewriting compresses, not what it translates). Arm: {W_scaf, W_temp} x {C_v7, C_r3} for R1 at 8 seeds.
- P5 (token-matched, absolute): S(C_r3) - S(C_v7) >= M with CI excluding 0 in the cell (W_other,R1) and >= M_R2 with CI excluding 0 in the cell (W_self,R2). Falsifier: the CI includes 0 or is negative in either cell (seven verbatim foreign items at greater token cost do as well as three rewritten ones). Arm: those four cells at 8 seeds; Measurement C shows k7 is not harmed relative to k3 for R1, so the comparator is a strong one.
- P6 (placebo, absolute): D(W_far,R1) - [S(R1,C_pl_static) - S(R1,static3)] >= M with CI excluding 0, tested only if S(R1,C_r3,W_far) - S(R1,C_v7,W_far) has a CI excluding 0; and S(R1,C_pl_mis) - S(R1,static3) has a 95% CI upper bound below M. Falsifier: the placebo difference-of-differences has a CI including 0 (rewriting fixed exemplars into a plan captures the increment: it is a planning step, not adaptation of the foreign item), or the mismatched rewrite gains >= M (rewriting anything helps). Arm: C_pl_static, C_pl_mis, static3 and the W_far cells for R1 at 8 seeds.
- P7 (symmetry across the store): D(W_self,R2) - D(W_other,R2) >= M_R2 with CI excluding 0, i.e. the same two banks with the roles of foreign and own reversed for EXAONE. Falsifier: CI includes 0 or negative (rewriting does not help EXAONE read Qwen3's experience more than it helps it read its own). Arm: {W_self, W_other} x {C_v7, C_r3} for R2 at 8 seeds, with R2's own static3 and self-pool cells.
- P8 (translation, not compression): with both headline banks capped at 2x the expert median length, D(W_far^cap,R1) - D(W_self^cap,R1) >= M with CI excluding 0. Falsifier: the capped CI includes 0 while the uncapped P1 contrast excluded it (the P1 increment was compression of long foreign items). Arm: {W_self^cap, W_far^cap} x {C_v7, C_r3} for R1 at 8 seeds.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired per-game success differences on the 274 evaluation games (seen + unseen, as in Measurement C) with seeds nested in games; cluster bootstrap over games (2,000 resamples) for every estimand, every difference-of-differences and every ratio. Seeds: 8 for every cell that enters P1-P8 (paired half-width ~+/-4 net for a single difference and ~+/-5.7 for a difference of two paired differences if noise scales as 1/sqrt(seeds) from the measured +/-8 at 274 x 2). The realized half-widths are computed first and M = max(G0/3, h_DiD) is set from them, so no prediction's margin can sit inside its own CI; if h_DiD at 8 seeds exceeds 7 net the four P1 cells go to 12 seeds, and if it still exceeds 8 the interaction is reported as underpowered and the absolute per-cell increments (P5) are the reportable result. Screening and exploratory cells ((W_exp,R2), C0 for R2, bank verification, the two 4-seed ablations) at 2-4 seeds (+/-8 to +/-5.7). One pre-registered headline contrast (P1); P2-P8 secondary, reported with unadjusted CIs and a Holm-adjusted summary; per-type breakdowns exploratory only (a ~45-game type cell has a half-width ~2.5x the pooled one and supports no claim). Margins are fractions of the measured Gate-0 gain (k7 - static3 = +19.5 for the expert bank; W_other's gain measured in Gate 0), never fixed numbers. Consumer-side tokens (prompt and generated, including the rewrite call) and episodes/min are logged per episode and reported per cell, so every increment carries its token cost. Readers run at temperature 0; writers at the temperature their manipulation specifies; seeds fix the environment split and sampling. All runs under nohup with pid files and append-only JSONL, workers tuned to the vLLM running queue (>= 8 per replica), one replica per A100, both GPUs busy throughout.
Preprint Collision Check: All queries ran through tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, channel s2=ok hf=ok unless noted). Nearest pre-emption is AdaCoM's reader-strength dependence; it does not vary the writer and does not compare against verbatim injection at matched tokens. No result found that reports the adaptation increment as a function of writer identity.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Ceiling: verbatim expert items give R1 ~0.81/0.87 success at k=3 and k7 - static3 = +19.5, leaving 13-19 net of headroom for reconstruction on W_exp; the headline therefore rests on W_other (Gate 0 requires its verbatim k=7 gain net of static3 to be >= +12 with CI excluding 0), with W_exp as the pre-registered fallback whose ceiling then bounds the increment and is reported as such. Name: rewriter_trained_against_one_reader_matched_cost
Title: A Rewriter Learned Against One Reader Is That Reader's: Net-Point Transfer of Execution-Trained Experience Rewriters Across Scaffold, Capability and Backbone, Against Self-Collection at Equal GPU-Hours
Short Hypothesis: An experience rewriter trained by execution-feedback rejection sampling against one reader is that reader's: moved to a different 32B backbone at matched k=0 success it loses at least half of its increment over token-matched verbatim injection (at least 6 net points), moved to the same backbone under a different scaffold it keeps the increment within 6 net, and moved to the same backbone in thinking mode it loses less than the backbone swap does, so reader specificity follows policy proximity rather than capability; and for the held-out backbone, the rewriter's training GPU-hours spent on collecting that backbone's own bank buy at least as much success (non-inferior at 5 net) as importing the foreign-trained rewriter.
Related Work: Model-aware skill alignment (2605.30723) trains a lightweight rewriter per backbone and reports that skills must be adapted to each backbone, but never applies a rewriter trained against one backbone to another, never reports how much of the gain is retained, and does not cost the evolution search against self-collection. SkillRevise (2606.01139) claims revised skills carry generalized procedural knowledge that transfers across models, the opposite prediction, without quantifying what is retained or a matched-cost comparison. CLEAR (2604.07487) trains a context augmentation model by contrastive reflection, SFT and RL against one execution agent and does not test another. AdaCoM (2605.30785) finds the right compression level for a frozen agent's own context depends on that agent's baseline strength, a hint that context artifacts are reader-specific, but it is not a foreign-experience rewriter and reports no held-out reader. HarnessDev (2609.01437) reports self-built harnesses transfer poorly across models. In the home literature, prompt transfer across model sizes has a transferability metric (PANDA 2208.10160) and MePO (2505.09930) claims model-agnostic prompt merits; the question of whether an execution-grounded rewriter is model-agnostic is open. Archived closer_beats_stronger concerned raw memory transfer, not a learned transfer component, and did not separate proximity from capability.
Abstract: Learned transfer components (rewriters, context augmentation models, memory composers) are trained against one consumer and assumed to serve others. We measure, in net success points with cluster-bootstrap CIs, how much of a rewriter's increment survives a change of reader, with the reader manipulated along three separated axes. Two rewriters, both QLoRA adapters on Qwen3-32B trained on equal-size pair sets, are learned on ALFWorld training games by rejection sampling: candidate rewrites of k=3 items retrieved from one shared store (expert, EXAONE-4.0-32B and Qwen3-32B banks) are executed by the in-loop reader, and rewrites that turn a verbatim failure into a success are kept as SFT targets; R_A is trained against Qwen3-32B under the standard scaffold, R_B against EXAONE-4.0-32B. Each rewriter is evaluated on four readers: its training reader, the same backbone under a plan-then-act scaffold (proximity at fixed capability), the same backbone in thinking mode with the budget tuned so k=0 sits 8-12 net above the standard reader (capability at fixed backbone, with a ceiling guard), and the other backbone at verified matched k=0 (backbone). Comparators on every reader are verbatim injection at matched consumer tokens (C_vtok, the smallest k whose tokens cover the rewriter's plan), a training-free prompted rewriter at three decoding budgets, a no-execution-filter adapter, the rewriter given no item (memory-absent) or wrong-type items (mismatched), and for the held-out backbone its own bank enlarged by the episode-equivalent of the rewriter's training GPU-hours. The increment I(R,r) = S(r,R) - S(r,C_vtok) and its differences across readers are the estimands; the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader is reported alongside. Gate 0 requires I(R_A,A) and I(R_B,B) >= 10 net at 274 games x 8 seeds. Every margin is a pre-registered absolute net-point threshold at or above the half-width of the cells that carry it (5 net for within-reader contrasts at 8 seeds, 6 net for cross-reader contrasts), with the fractional readings (half, two thirds of the Gate-0 increment) applied as floors, and the matched-cost claim is a non-inferiority test. The claims fail if the foreign-trained rewriter is within 5 net of the reader-trained one on either reader, if the thinking-mode reader loses more than the other backbone, if the memory-absent rewriter keeps most of the gain, or if the imported rewriter beats equal-cost self-collection by 5 net.
Experiments:
- Store: S = W_exp (expert) + W_EXA (EXAONE-4.0-32B successes, one pass over the 3,553 training games) + W_QW (Qwen3-32B successes, one pass at the same episode budget), the same store read by every reader and used for all rewriter training; W_QW-only and W_EXA-only cells are the self-pool and writer-specific cells; W_EXA+ (matched-cost bank) is extra EXAONE collection whose episode count is fixed before any B cell as R_A's logged training GPU-hours x the measured EXAONE episodes/GPU-h (expected ~4.8 GPU-h x 1,200 = ~5,800 episodes).
- Readers: A Qwen3-32B standard ReAct scaffold, non-thinking, T=0; A' Qwen3-32B plan-then-act scaffold, T=0 (proximity; verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A); A'' Qwen3-32B thinking mode, thinking budget tuned on the C0 cell so k=0 sits 8-12 net above A (capability at fixed backbone; ceiling guard: no A'' cell may exceed 85% success, else the budget is lowered and the cell rerun); B EXAONE-4.0-32B standard scaffold (verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A; if not, B is reported as a joint backbone-and-capability change and P2a/P2b are restated with A'' as the only capability reader). gpt-oss-120b is dropped: it carried no prediction.
- Rewriter training: 1,000 training games; 3 candidate rewrites per game from the prompted Qwen3-32B rewriter R_0 at T=0.8 (input: task, first observation, k=3 items from S; output: one plan in the reader's action format); each candidate and the verbatim k=3 context executed by the in-loop reader (4,000 episodes, ~3.3 GPU-h at 20/min); keep rewrites where the reader succeeded and verbatim failed plus a 1:1 share of success-success pairs; the R_A and R_B pair sets are subsampled to equal size; QLoRA r=32, one epoch (~1.5 GPU-h). Same recipe for R_B with B in the loop; rewriter backbone Qwen3-32B for both so only the in-loop reader differs. R_nf (no filter): the same adapter recipe on one random candidate per game from R_A's candidate set, same pair count (no execution, ~1.5 GPU-h).
- C_vtok rule: verbatim injection from S at the smallest k whose consumer tokens are >= the rewriter's median plan length (expected k=1: +9.1 over static3 in Measurement C; k=3 is +17.2, k=7 is +19.5).
- Cells (274 games x seeds): reader A: C0 (2), C_static = static3 (4), C_v3 (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8), C_RB (8), C_Rnf (4), C_R0g prompted rewriter greedy (8), C_R0s prompted rewriter one T=0.8 sample (4), C_R0b3 three T=0.8 samples chosen by a self-selection prompt (4), C_RA_empty task and no item (8), C_RA_mis wrong-type items planted at 3/3 (4), C_self W_QW-only k=3 (4), C_v3[W_EXA] (8), C_RA[W_EXA] (8) = 86 seed-cells, 23.6k episodes. Reader A': C0 (2), C_static (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8) = 22, 6.0k. Reader A'': C0 plus budget tuning (4), C_static (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8) = 24, 6.6k at ~10/min. Reader B: C0 (2), C_static (4), C_v3 (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8), C_RB (8), C_Rnf (4), C_selfcost = S + W_EXA+ verbatim at k=3 (8) and at k=7 (4), C_half = S with W_EXA halved at k=3 (2, bank-size slope), C_v3[W_EXA] (4), C_v3[W_QW] (4), C_RB[W_QW] (4) = 64, 17.5k. Total ~53.7k evaluation episodes, ~50 GPU-h; training ~11 GPU-h (two in-loop rewriters, one no-filter adapter); collection ~11 GPU-h (W_QW, W_EXA, W_EXA+); ~72 GPU-h on two A100s = ~36 h packed, about 3 days with serving changes.
- Estimands: g(r,cond) = S(r,cond) - S(r,C_static); I(R,r) = S(r,R) - S(r,C_vtok) (the adaptation step against direct injection at matched tokens); reader-specificity differences D_B = S(B,C_RB) - S(B,C_RA) and D_A = S(A,C_RA) - S(A,C_RB); transfer losses I(R_A,A) - I(R_A,r) for r in A', A'', B, with the fraction I(R_A,r)/I(R_A,A) reported with joint-bootstrap CIs but never used as a threshold; retained-gain ratio per writer x reader (g(A,C_v3[W_EXA]) / g(B,C_v3[W_EXA]) and its rewritten counterpart g(A,C_RA[W_EXA]) / g(B,C_v3[W_EXA]); g(B,C_v3[W_QW]) / g(A,C_self) and g(B,C_RB[W_QW]) / g(A,C_self) likewise); consumer tokens per episode (rewriter output counted) and episodes/min; training GPU-hours per rewriter.
- Gate 0: I(R_A,A) >= 10 net with lower 95% bound > 0 and I(R_B,B) >= 10 net likewise, at 274 x 8 seeds, before any held-out cell. With C_vtok = k1 this asks the rewriter's ~300-token plan to reach the k=7 verbatim level (+19.5 over static3) at about one fifth of the consumer tokens. A rewriter with 5 <= I < 10 runs the same cells with the absolute margins but the fractional readings are reported as underpowered; I < 5 is reported as a null and R_0 (greedy) becomes the transferred subject for P2 and P4 only.
- Order: C_static and C_R0g on A first; then R_A training and Gate 0; then B, A', A'' cells; the matched-cost and W_EXA/W_QW cells last.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest first: C_static (static3, the Measurement-C best static arm), then C_R0g (prompted rewriter, no training) before any trained cell.
- Direct injection of the unmodified items at matched consumer tokens (C_vtok) is the comparator inside every increment; C_v3 and, for B, k=7 are reported as the information-matched and best-verbatim comparators, so the rewriter is scored against both fewer tokens and more information.
- Self-pool control at matched collection cost: C_self (W_QW-only, one pass at W_EXA's episode budget) for A, C_v3[W_EXA] for B; C_selfcost converts R_A's logged training GPU-hours into EXAONE episodes at the measured rate and is read at k=3 (primary, the rewriter's own item count) and k=7 (secondary, best k in Measurement C); C_half gives the bank-size slope so a flat curve is visible rather than assumed.
- Memory-absent (C_RA_empty), matched (training reader) and mismatched (C_RA_mis, wrong-type items planted at 3/3, the rewriter analogue of Measurement C's blind1 placebo; and the held-out readers) evaluation of each trained component.
- Prompted rewriter at three budgets (greedy; one T=0.8 sample, the distribution R_A was distilled from; best-of-3 T=0.8 samples chosen by a self-selection prompt at 3x rewriter tokens) so that P5 is not decided by decoding.
- Mechanism ablation: R_nf, the same adapter recipe with no execution filter, scored on A and B; if R_nf shows the same D_A and D_B as the filtered rewriters, reader specificity comes from the candidate generator rather than from the in-loop reader and the mechanism claim fails.

Name: shared_blind_spot
Title: Shared Blind Spots: A Reader Is Most Harmed by, and Least Able to Detect, Contaminated Experience Written by Its Own Policy
Short Hypothesis: Contamination in an experience bank propagates in proportion to writer-reader policy proximity: failed trajectories relabelled as successes are more harmful per planted item and less detectable at read time when written by the reader's own policy or a same-backbone near variant than when written by a distant backbone, because read-time detection is the reader's own plausibility judgment, which endorsed those actions when it produced them. Consequences that the design tests: the harm ordering reverses when the reader is swapped (self > far for each reader, so it is proximity, not a property of any writer's failures); a judge from a different backbone detects a writer's masked failures better than the writer's own backbone does (a diagonal deficit in the judge x writer table) and the deficit survives when the failed terminal state is visible but the failure label is not; filtering the bank by a foreign judge recovers harm that filtering by the reader's own judgment cannot; manufactured wrong-procedure grafts (positive control) are harmful regardless of writer.
Related Work: MemoryGraft (arXiv:2512.16962) implants attacker-written 'successful experiences' and shows persistent drift on one backbone; the Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608) diagnoses how agents consume conflicting memory along a trajectory and finds stronger agents are harmed more, varying the reader but not the writer and without a read-time detector; MemAudit (arXiv:2605.23723) audits poisoned memory post hoc by causal attribution; forensic trajectory signatures (arXiv:2606.30566), Bayesian trust scoring (arXiv:2603.02240) and provenance gating (arXiv:2608.10509) defend against adversarial injection; collective false memories (arXiv:2602.00428) leave the introducer's capability gap untested; 2605.22842 shows memory-layer misconduct is misattributed to model failure. None plants natural, non-adversarial failures by writer identity or measures the reader's own recall against a foreign judge's. In the home literature of self-training, confirmation bias in pseudo-labeling is countered by a second model's disagreement or ensemble diversity (arXiv:2310.14814, arXiv:2403.03095 cross pseudo-labeling), which is the parametric analog of the cross-judge arm. The archived idea lineage_blast_radius (4.75) was judged entailed by its consolidation rule; this design has no consolidation rule, plants contamination at a controlled rate against a fixed-recipe positive control and a placebo, and measures precision/recall.
Abstract: Population and cross-model memory stores mix experience from many writers, and the literature asserts rather than measures whether a writer's errors propagate to a reader and whether the reader can tell. We manufacture contamination with writer identity as the manipulated variable: the same 274 evaluation games, the same 1,200-item expert walkthrough bank (reader Qwen3-32B; the clean gain is replicated as the rate-0 cell) and the same retriever, with 50 percent of the bank replaced by type-matched, length-matched contaminants of one writer. Contaminants are failed training trajectories relabelled as successes (truncated at the last coherent action, failure line removed, success line appended; coherence-filtered) from five writers on a measured proximity axis: the reader's own policy (Q-self), two same-backbone variants at matched k=0 success and lower action agreement (Q-prox-T: temperature; Q-prox-S: scaffold), EXAONE-4.0-32B (E-self, the pre-registered foreign comparator) and gpt-oss-120b (G-self, secondary). A fixed-recipe wrong-procedure graft on expert items is the writer-agnostic positive control and a length-matched truncated clean placebo bounds truncation harm. Every confirmatory estimand is a paired difference between two contaminated cells at 12 seeds (half-width about 3.3 net), so the clean base cancels; the retained fraction of the clean gain rho_c is reported per writer x reader cell with CIs. The two primary contaminated banks are also read by EXAONE as a second reader (mirror). Read-time detection is scored offline as precision and recall in a full judge x writer table (Q, E and G judging every writer's items) at a matched false-rejection rate, on the same 600 items per writer at three evidence levels: masked, state-visible (failure line removed but the failed terminal state kept) and unmasked. Two filter cells at 50 percent apply the reader's own judgment or the foreign judge to the bank before the run. We predict that the reader's own failures harm it by at least 5 net more than the foreign comparator's, that the ordering reverses for the second reader, that same-backbone near variants are less harmful by at least 4 net (proximity, not backbone), a diagonal deficit of at least 0.15 recall in the judge x writer table that persists at 0.08 or more when the failed state is visible without the label, and that the foreign-judge filter recovers at least 5 net more harm than the own-judgment filter. The result would make writer identity, not just content, a required field for any read-time filter, and would identify the reader's own past failures as the worst-case contaminant in a shared store.
Experiments: Reader Q = Qwen3-32B (primary); E = EXAONE-4.0-32B as second reader, pre-registered foreign comparator and cross-judge (Gate V: serves in vLLM 0.13 and k=0 >= 0.30; if E fails Gate V the comparator and cross-judge become G and the capability confound at the far end is reported); G = gpt-oss-120b as secondary far writer and third judge if it serves. Evaluation: 274 games (seen/unseen halves), paired by game and seed across every arm. Bank: N = 1,200 expert walkthrough items (200 per type) from the Measurement-A pool; retrieval unchanged (task-description embedding, k = 3). Gate B (pilot, 2 seeds, before confirmatory cells): the 1,200-item clean bank retains >= +10 net over static3 (expected near the measured +17.2); otherwise the bank is enlarged once to 2,000 items. Contamination at rate 0.5 replaces 600 items (100 per type) with type-matched contaminants of one writer; rate 0 is the clean base. Writer pools: Q-self failures on disk (1,661 of 3,553 training games); Q-prox-T (same backbone and scaffold, sampling temperature raised until pi drops by >= 0.15), Q-prox-S (same backbone and temperature, alternative ReAct template with thinking disabled) and E-self collected on 2,000 training games (333 per type) each; G-self on all 3,553 because G fails rarely; about 9,500 writer episodes on GPU1 during day 1. Proximity pi(W) = agreement between reader Q's greedy k=0 action and writer W's greedy action on 300 fixed probe states drawn from Q's own k=0 trajectories (writer policies queried on the reader's states; for Q-self the writer is the reader's collection policy). Manipulation check per Q-prox variant, run before its cells: pi(Q-prox) <= pi(Q-self) - 0.15 and k=0 success within +/-3 net of Q-self; a failing variant is re-calibrated once (temperature) or dropped. Masking (L0): failure truncated at the last coherent action, terminal failure line removed, a success line appended; coherence filter (<= 2 'Nothing happens', >= 1 correct object interaction); item length matched across writers by selection, distribution reported. Graded-evidence variants of the same items: L1 keeps the full trajectory to its true end (failing final steps and terminal observation visible), failure line removed, success line appended; L2 = L1 plus the terminal failure line. Graft v1 (fixed recipe): expert items with the procedure block rotated (heat -> cool -> clean -> heat: microwave, fridge, sinkbasin steps) for the three procedure types, the final placement redirected to a wrong receptacle for pick and pick-two, and the lamp step deleted for look; success line intact. Graft v2 (the only permitted re-specification, run only if v1 fails Gate 0): v1 plus a same-category distractor object substituted throughout. Placebo: clean expert items truncated to the contaminant length distribution, success line intact. Filters: each judge (memory-free, asked whether the trajectory completes its stated task, 1-5 confidence) scores all 1,200 bank items offline at the operating point where it rejects 5 percent of the clean expert items; rejected items are removed before the run. Reader-Q cells (episodes = 274 x seeds): k=0 (2 seeds, 548); static3 (2, 548); clean expert bank (8, 2,192); Q-self 50 (12, 3,288); E-self 50 (12, 3,288); Q-prox-T 50 (6, 1,644); Q-prox-S 50 (6, 1,644); G-self 50 (4, 1,096); graft v1 50 (8, 2,192); placebo 50 (8, 2,192); own-judgment filter on Q-self 50 (8, 2,192); cross-judge filter on Q-self 50 (8, 2,192); clean self-pool base at matched collection cost (2, 548): 23,564 episodes. Reader-E cells: k=0, static3, clean expert bank (2 seeds each, 1,644); E + Q-self 50 (6, 1,644); E + E-self 50 (6, 1,644): 4,932. Contingent: graft v2 (8, 2,192). Total 28,496 reader episodes (30,688 with v2) plus about 9,500 writer episodes. Detection: judge x writer table on the 600 bank contaminants per writer at L0, L1 and L2, plus 600 clean expert and 600 clean self items for false-rejection calibration and a memory-absent set (no item: must abstain): 5 writers x 600 x 3 levels x 2-3 judges plus calibration, about 30,000 short judgments, 4-6 GPU-hours. Schedule: day 1, GPU0 runs the Q cells that need no new pool (k=0, static3, clean, Q-self, graft, placebo, own filter, self-pool base: 13,700 episodes) while GPU1 collects the four writer pools and then scores the cross filter; days 2-3, GPU0 runs the remaining Q cells (9,864) while GPU1 serves E for the reader-E cells (4,932) and the detection table, then both GPUs serve Q for whatever remains. About 3 days on two A100s, both busy throughout; throughput and vLLM queue depth reported per phase. Analysis: paired contrasts between contaminated cells (the clean base cancels), game-level bootstrap CIs, rho_c per cell, Wilson and item-paired bootstrap intervals for the detection table. Gate 0: the graft (v1 or v2) or Q-self costs >= 6 net at 50 percent with a CI excluding zero; if neither does, the reader is reported as insensitive to 50 percent contamination at k=3 and P1, P2 and P5 as untestable on it. Pre-registration of the cell list, seeds, margins, graft recipes, coherence filter, pi definition, Gates 0, B and V before the first confirmatory cell. Optional extension only if time remains: Q-self and E-self at rate 1.0 (2 seeds each) for a harm slope.
Baselines and Ablations: Clean expert bank (rate 0, replicates Measurement A on the 1,200-item bank) and clean self bank at matched collection cost (rate 0; denominators for rho_c and the brief's self-pool control); static3 (Measurement C's best static arm) and k=0 for both readers, so every gain and harm is reported net of the fixed procedure prompt; length-matched truncated clean placebo at 50 percent separating contamination from truncation; graft v1 positive control with a single named re-specification v2, both reported; graded-evidence levels L0/L1/L2 on the same items (in place of a masked/unmasked pair) so the deficit is measured off ceiling; terminal-line regex detector as the cheapest read-time filter (recall 1 at L2 and 0 at L0/L1 by construction, reported for scale); own-judgment vs cross-judge filter at 50 percent, with the offline removed fractions of contaminants and of clean items per filter; judge x writer table with memory-absent (must abstain), matched and mismatched evaluation and false-rejection calibrated on clean items; proximity manipulation check (pi and k=0) for each same-backbone variant, and E-self vs G-self as the capability contrast at measured pi (descriptive); reader-E mirror cells (the same two contaminated banks read by a second reader); laundering check (offline): the reader's re-rationalization pass applied to masked self failures, reporting the fraction that afterwards read as successes to each judge (adaptation propagates or filters); seen vs unseen halves; realized contaminant share of the injected context per episode.
Falsifiable Predictions:
P1 (headline: self-written failures are the worst contaminant): for reader Q at 50 percent, D_Q = S(E-self cell) - S(Q-self cell) = harm(Q-self) - harm(E-self), a single paired difference of two 12-seed cells (the clean base cancels), half-width about 3.3 net. Pre-registered comparator: E-self (G-self is a secondary replication, D_G at 4 vs 12 seeds, half-width 4.6, reported, not substituted). Predicted: D_Q >= 5 net with the 95 percent CI excluding zero, and harm(Q-self) >= 6 net against the clean base (12 vs 8 seeds, half-width 3.65). Falsified if the CI upper bound of D_Q is below 5 net (point below about 1.7: foreign failures harm as much, more, or nearly as much); falsified in its premise if harm(Q-self) has an upper bound below 6 while the graft passes Gate 0 (relabelled natural failures do not propagate on this reader, only manufactured wrong procedures do); a D_G whose CI lies entirely below zero is reported as contrary evidence. Reader-E mirror (reader-E cells, 6 seeds each, half-width 4.6): D_E = S_E(Q-self cell) - S_E(E-self cell) predicted positive; if D_E's CI lies entirely below zero the proximity account is falsified even when D_Q passes, because Q-self items would then harm any reader (a writer property, not proximity). Not entailed: a distant backbone's failures (invalid-command loops, over-long analysis) could plausibly be more disruptive to imitate, and both writers are equally far from the expert items in style.
P2 (proximity, not backbone, at fixed capability): Q-prox-T and Q-prox-S each pass the manipulation check (pi(Q-prox) <= pi(Q-self) - 0.15; k=0 success within +/-3 net of Q-self) before their cells run. Predicted: pooled Q-prox at 50 percent (2 x 6 seeds) is less harmful than Q-self by >= 4 net, contrast S(Q-prox) - S(Q-self) with half-width about 3.3, and more harmful than E-self (S(E-self) - S(Q-prox) > 0, reported with CI); descriptively, the weighted slope of harm on measured pi over the five writers (pi axis spanning >= 0.3) is >= 8 net per unit pi with a game-level bootstrap CI excluding zero. Falsified if S(Q-prox) - S(Q-self) has an upper bound below 4 net (a same-backbone policy at lower agreement harms as much as the reader's own: identity is the backbone, not the policy, and the proximity mechanism is wrong), or if the slope's CI includes zero while D_Q passes (the harm difference is a backbone step, not a gradient). If only one variant passes the check the contrast uses it alone at 6 seeds (half-width 4.6) with margin 5; if neither passes, P2 is reported as unmanipulated, not as confirmed.
P3 (diagonal deficit): in the judge x writer recall table on L0 masked items (600 per writer) at a matched false-rejection rate of 5 percent on clean items, deficit_Q = recall(E judges Q-self) - recall(Q judges Q-self) and deficit_E = recall(Q judges E-self) - recall(E judges E-self) are each >= 0.15 (two-cell SE about 0.029, so about 5 SE), tested as the judge x writer interaction with each judge's overall recall as a covariate; Q judging Q-prox items is predicted between Q judging Q-self and Q judging E-self (descriptive). Falsified if either deficit has a 95 percent CI upper bound below 0.05 (a writer's masked failures are as detectable by its own backbone as by a foreign one), including the case where one judge is uniformly better in every column; produced by the offline detection table. Not entailed: an item's detectability could be a property of its text alone, which would appear as a writer main effect, not an interaction.
P4 (the blind spot is judgment of the actions, not the appended label): the same 600 items per writer are scored at L0 (masked), L1 (full trajectory to its true end with the failed terminal state visible, failure line removed, success line appended) and L2 (L1 plus the failure line), item-paired. P5 (the foreign judge's filter recovers harm the own filter cannot): filters applied offline to the 50 percent Q-self bank at the matched 5 percent false-rejection point, then the filtered bank is run (8 seeds each). Falsified for the placebo if S(placebo) - S(Q-self) has an upper bound below 4 net (truncation, not content, accounts for the harm) or if the placebo's own cost has a lower bound above 6 (truncated clean items are themselves contaminants at Gate-0 scale). Margins are pre-registered above the half-width and as fractions of the Gate-0 effect (6 net): P1 5 net, P2 4 net, P5 5 and 6 net, P6 4 net. Decision rule per contrast: confirmed if the point estimate meets the margin and the 95 percent CI excludes zero; falsified if the CI upper bound lies below the margin; otherwise reported as underpowered with the interval. Detection: n = 600 items per writer, Wilson SE about 0.02 per recall and about 0.029 for a two-cell difference, so the 0.15 deficit is about 5 SE; the L0/L1/L2 comparisons are item-paired (the same 600 items at each level) with an item bootstrap, so the 0.08 persistence margin exceeds 2.5 paired SE; judges operate at a matched false-rejection rate (5 percent on 600 clean expert items) and are scored memory-absent (must abstain), so a judge that says 'no' to everything does not score; the diagonal-deficit test is pre-registered as the judge x writer interaction with each judge's overall recall as a covariate, so a uniformly better judge does not confirm it. Contamination rate is fixed at the bank level per type so the expected contaminant share of the injected context is equal across writers; the realized share per episode is logged and reported; contaminant length is matched across writers by selection and the placebo bounds the truncation component. Capability and proximity are separated: Q-prox varies pi at fixed backbone with k=0 within +/-3 of Q-self (manipulation-check gate), E-self vs G-self varies capability at measured pi (reported, descriptive). The clean base's residual over static3 is expected near the measured +17.2 (+/-5) and is gated at +10 (Gate B); rho_c = [S(contaminated) - S(static3)] / [S(clean) - S(static3)] is reported per writer x reader cell with CIs; consumer-side tokens per cell reported.
